name: Construction and trades
question_lede: Jobs arrive by phone and WhatsApp, pricing happens from site photos, and the paperwork waits until evening.

areas.name: Quotes and estimates
areas.pain: Quote requests arrive as WhatsApp photos and voice notes, typed up after hours.
areas.hook: Still typing up quotes at night from WhatsApp photos and voice notes?

services.name: Quote drafted from WhatsApp photos and voice notes
services.what: Photos, voice notes and messages sent to a WhatsApp Business number, your inbox or an upload form on your site land in one intake. Voice notes are transcribed, scope and quantities pulled out, and the quote drafted against your price list in your template.
services.human: You approve every quote before it is sent.

services.name: Quote follow-ups that stop on reply
services.what: A sent quote gets a scheduled follow-up sequence in templates you signed off. A customer reply stops it and lands in your inbox.
services.human: You choose the templates and the schedule; a reply always goes to you.

services.name: Quote filed to the job in your CRM
services.what: Every quote, its photos and the thread are filed against the customer and the job in Tradify, ServiceM8, Jobber or whatever you run, so nothing lives only in a phone.
services.human: Nothing is deleted or merged without your say.

services.name: Price book refreshed from paid invoices
services.what: Once invoice capture is in place, each price-book item is linked to the last price you paid, matched from the captured invoice lines through merchants' wording differences. When a merchant price moves, the quoting rate is flagged for update.
services.human: You decide whether a rate changes; the system only proposes.

areas.proof_note: Same mechanics: messy photos and scans in, validated records out. The client was a tournament data platform, not a contractor.

areas.name: Supplier invoices and deliveries
areas.pain: Invoices and delivery notes pile up as scans and phone photos until month end.
areas.hook: Still matching supplier invoices to jobs at month end, from a pile of photos?

services.name: Invoices and delivery notes read into job costs
services.what: Scanned invoices, delivery notes and photographed receipts are read by a vision model, matched to supplier and job through OCR noise, checked on quantities and totals, then posted to Xero, QuickBooks or Sage Accounting, or as an import file for Sage 50.
services.human: Documents that fail a check wait in a queue with the reason. You clear it, or a site manager does, within limits you set.

services.name: Delivery notes checked against the order
services.what: Where a purchase order was raised, each delivery note is compared with it line by line. Short deliveries and price differences are flagged the same day, not at invoice time.
services.human: You decide what to query with the supplier; the system only flags.

services.name: Purchase orders drafted from the quote
services.what: Material lines of a won quote are grouped by the usual supplier in your price list and drafted as purchase orders in Xero or QuickBooks, or as a numbered PDF for suppliers you phone. Delivery notes and invoices then have an order to match.
services.human: You pick the supplier and send each order. Nothing is ordered by the system.

services.name: Merchant statements reconciled to posted bills
services.what: Monthly statements from builders' merchants and hire companies are matched line by line to the bills already posted. Missing invoices, duplicates and credits not received are listed with the job they belong to.
services.human: Your bookkeeper works the list; nothing is posted or written off by the system.

services.name: Plant hire tracked from hire and off-hire notes
services.what: On-hire and off-hire notes from email, PDFs and a dedicated WhatsApp number are read into a live hire register per job, so equipment still on hire after the job closes is flagged before the invoice arrives.
services.human: The site manager confirms off-hire; the register only flags.

areas.proof_note: 412 records, 0 validation errors on mixed PDFs and scans, with a hard validation gate. Built for tournament data, not construction.

areas.name: Job costing and reporting
areas.pain: Which jobs actually made money is a question for the accountant, months later.
areas.hook: Still finding out which jobs made money from the accountant, months later?

services.name: Margin per job, refreshed every night
services.what: Quotes, supplier costs and timesheets from Xero or QuickBooks, your job tool and your timesheet app, pulled nightly into SQL Server with margin per job. Reconciled against your accounting totals before anyone relies on it.
services.human: You and your bookkeeper sign off the reconciliation before cutover. The report is read-only.

services.name: Monday numbers in your inbox
services.what: A short scheduled report: jobs quoted, won, in progress, invoiced and overdue, with the numbers linked to their source. No dashboard to log into.
services.human: You read it. The system changes nothing in your books.

services.name: Cost to complete per live job
services.what: Committed orders, costs to date and the remaining budget per job, by cost code, refreshed from the same tables, so an overrun shows while the job is open. Needs cost codes and purchase orders in your systems; without them, start with margin per job.
services.human: The contracts manager decides what to do; the view only shows.

services.name: Power BI across jobs, sites and trades
services.what: Dashboards on the fact tables: margin by job type, labour against estimate, supplier spend by trade and retention outstanding, with scheduled refresh so the number on screen is the number in the database.
services.human: You decide the metrics; definitions are written down once.

services.name: Estimate against actual, by trade and cost code
services.what: When a job closes, the estimate is compared with what the job cost in labour and materials, by trade and cost code, since that is how costs are booked. Codes that are consistently under-priced are listed by job type.
services.human: You decide whether to change the rates; the comparison only informs.

areas.proof_note: 68,890 orders reconciled across 25 audited columns for a retailer's finance team. Same reconciliation work, different industry.

areas.name: Tenders and take-offs
areas.pain: Tender packs are hundreds of pages, and quantities are still counted off drawings by hand.
areas.hook: Still reading tender packs page by page and counting quantities off drawings by hand?

services.name: Tender pack summarised to scope, dates and risks
services.what: The ITT, specification, preliminaries and contract terms are read into a fixed summary: scope by trade, submission deadline, site constraints, payment terms, liquidated damages and anything unusual, each item linked to its page.
services.human: The estimator reads the summary and decides whether to bid. The pack is never skipped.

services.name: Schedules and quantity tables read off tender drawings
services.what: Door, window, finishes and sanitaryware schedules, and quantity tables printed on the drawings, are read by a vision model into a quantities list per element, each tied to its sheet. Nothing is counted or measured off the plan itself; that stays in your take-off tool.
services.human: The estimator checks every count against the drawing before it is priced.

services.name: Bill of quantities priced from your rate library
services.what: A BoQ in Excel or CITE format is matched item by item to your rate library and the last three jobs that used it, with unmatched items listed for the estimator.
services.human: The estimator prices the unmatched items and signs off the bill. No rate is applied without a match.

services.name: Tender questions and addenda tracked
services.what: Clarifications sent, answers received and addenda issued are logged against the tender from your tender inbox and the portal's notification emails, with the deadline moved when an addendum moves it.
services.human: The bid lead decides what to ask; the log only records.

services.name: Subcontractor quotes compared on one sheet
services.what: Quotes from subcontractors arrive as PDFs in different layouts. Each is read into the same line structure, exclusions and provisional sums are called out, and a comparison sheet is built per package.
services.human: You choose the subcontractor; the sheet shows what each quote leaves out.

areas.proof_note: Vision extraction from mixed PDFs and scans with a hard validation gate: 412 records, 0 errors. Tournament data, not drawings or tender packs.

areas.name: Site diaries and progress
areas.pain: Progress lives in WhatsApp groups and the diary gets written up on Friday from memory.
areas.hook: Still writing up the site diary on Friday from a week of WhatsApp photos?

services.name: Daily site diary drafted from a site number
services.what: The site sends photos, voice notes and messages to a dedicated WhatsApp Business number (group chats cannot be read). Each evening they become a dated diary entry per job: who was on site, work done, deliveries, weather, delays, filed to Procore, Fieldwire or your drive.
services.human: The site manager reads and signs the entry each day. Nothing is filed unsigned.

services.name: Progress photos sorted by job, area and date
services.what: Each photo is filed to job, area and element from its caption, who sent it and what a vision model sees, then stored in folders you can search. Caption leads; vision alone does not file.
services.human: A person confirms low-confidence matches once; the rule is then remembered.

services.name: Snagging list built from photos and voice notes
services.what: Defects captured on the walk-round as photos and voice notes, sent to the site number or logged in Fieldwire, become a numbered snag list with location, trade and description, assigned to the subcontractor and closed with a photo.
services.human: The site manager assigns and closes each snag. The list never closes one itself.

services.name: Variations caught before they are forgotten
services.what: Messages to the site number and emails that read like a change to scope are flagged, a variation record is drafted with the instruction, the date and the photos, and it waits to be priced.
services.human: The contracts manager prices it and decides whether to claim it. Nothing is sent to the client.

services.name: Hours on site read into timesheets
services.what: Hours sent as a WhatsApp message, a photo of the sheet or a clock-in app export are read per person per job per day, checked against site-access logs where you have them, and passed to payroll.
services.human: Mismatches wait for the site manager. Payroll never receives an unchecked hour.

services.name: Progress against programme, from diary and photos
services.what: Diary entries and photos are tied to activities in your programme, read from an Asta Powerproject, MS Project (MPP) or Primavera P6 (XER) export, not a live link. Each activity shows last evidence of work and days of drift; a weekly client report is drafted.
services.human: The project manager updates the programme and sends the report. The system only proposes status.

areas.proof_note: Scheduled narrative from several live sources, every line linked to its origin: the analytics agent, built for a marketing team, not a site.

areas.name: Drawings, RFIs and handover
areas.pain: Which drawing revision is current, and who owes the RFI answer, lives in email threads.
areas.hook: Still finding out the site built off a superseded drawing after the fact?

services.name: Drawing register kept current from issued PDFs
services.what: Drawings arrive by issue email, as a download from Procore or Autodesk Construction Cloud, or in a shared folder. Number, title, revision and date are read from each title block, the register updated, superseded sheets flagged and the site told which drawings changed.
services.human: The document controller confirms each new revision before the site is told.

services.name: Superseded drawings on site caught from a photo
services.what: A phone photo of any sheet in the site cabin is read for its number and revision and checked against the register. Out-of-date sheets are flagged back by message, with the current revision named. Needs the register above.
services.human: The site manager decides what to do with the sheet; the reply only flags.

services.name: RFIs and submittals logged with an owner
services.what: RFIs and technical submittals raised or answered by email, or through Procore or Aconex notification emails, are logged against the job with date raised, who owes the answer, days open and the drawings affected. A weekly open list goes to the project manager.
services.human: The project manager chases; the log only records and reminds.

services.name: Handover pack assembled from filed documents
services.what: Test certificates, commissioning sheets, warranties, product data and as-built drawings already filed per job are read, matched to the handover index you use, and assembled into the O&M pack, with missing items listed per subcontractor so they can be chased before practical completion.
services.human: The project manager checks the pack and issues it. Nothing is sent to the client unreviewed.

areas.proof_note: Title blocks and certificates are the same job as the tournament scans: vision extraction, resolver, validation gate. Built for tournament data, not construction.

areas.name: Subcontractors and compliance
areas.pain: Method statements, insurance certificates and training cards are chased by email and expire unnoticed.
areas.hook: Still chasing subcontractors for insurance certificates and method statements by email?

services.name: Subcontractor onboarding pack checked on arrival
services.what: Insurance certificates, tax status, method statements and training cards arrive as PDFs and photos. Each is read, the expiry and cover amounts checked against your minimums, and the subcontractor record updated.
services.human: A document that fails a check waits for your compliance person with the reason.

services.name: Expiry chasing that stops when the document arrives
services.what: Thirty days before an insurance, licence or card expires, the subcontractor is asked for the renewal by email or WhatsApp, chased on a schedule, and the chase stops when a valid document is received.
services.human: You set the lead time and the wording. Nobody is blocked from site without a person deciding.

services.name: Method statements reviewed against your checklist
services.what: Each submitted method statement and risk assessment is read against your written checklist for that activity: missing hazards, missing controls, wrong site details. A review note is drafted for the manager.
services.human: The site manager accepts or rejects the submission. The note is advice.

services.name: Subcontractor applications checked before certifying
services.what: Each application for payment from a subcontractor, as a PDF or spreadsheet, is read into the same line structure, compared with the previous certified amount and with the diary's record of work done, and the differences listed for the quantity surveyor.
services.human: The quantity surveyor certifies every amount. The comparison only informs.

services.name: Subcontractor portal for documents and applications
services.what: A page where each subcontractor uploads certificates, method statements and payment applications, and sees what is missing, what has been certified and when retention is due. Documents are checked on upload; your compliance record and the retention ledger update. Next.js and FastAPI, EU-hosted on request.
services.human: Your team approves every document and certifies every amount. The portal collects and shows.

areas.proof_note: Checking every item against written rules, with the verdict and the rule recorded, is the creative pipeline, built for an education brand's ads.

areas.name: Payment applications and retentions
areas.pain: The monthly application is assembled from spreadsheets, and retentions are forgotten until the accountant asks.
areas.hook: Still building the monthly payment application from spreadsheets and forgetting the retentions?

services.name: Monthly application assembled from the job record
services.what: Work done to date, agreed variations and materials on site are pulled into your application template, with the previous certified amount carried forward. It draws on the site diary, the variation register and the cost tables, so those are built or exported first.
services.human: The quantity surveyor edits the amounts and submits. Nothing goes to the client unreviewed.

services.name: Payment certificates and notices read and compared
services.what: Payment certificates and pay-less notices arrive as PDFs. Each is read, the certified amount compared line by line with what was applied for, and the differences listed with the reason given.
services.human: You decide what to dispute and by when. The deadline is shown, never acted on.

services.name: Retention ledger, held and owed, with release dates
services.what: Retention held by clients on your applications and retention you hold on subcontractors, per job and party, in one ledger from Xero or QuickBooks, or a Sage export, plus the certificates and applications already read, with release dates and a reminder drafted when one passes.
services.human: You send the reminder and release the money. The ledger only shows and drafts.

services.name: Certified amounts chased past the final payment date
services.what: When a certified amount is not paid by the final date for payment on the certificate, a chase is drafted in your words with the certificate reference and amount, and any notice deadline shown. The sequence stops when the payment lands in your bank feed.
services.human: A person approves every chase. Replies land with you, not the system.

services.name: Cash flow by job, twelve weeks out
services.what: Applications due, certified amounts, supplier bills due and payroll, by week and by job, from the same reconciled tables, so the gap shows before the bank does.
services.human: You decide what to delay or chase. The forecast only shows.

areas.proof_note: Line-by-line parity against a legacy system, 68,890 orders across 25 columns, signed off with the client's QC team. A retailer, not a contractor.

areas.name: Enquiries and site visits
areas.pain: Missed calls and unanswered WhatsApps become someone else's job by the next morning.
areas.hook: Still losing jobs because the enquiry came in while you were on site?

services.name: Enquiries qualified and answered from one queue
services.what: Web form (with photo upload), WhatsApp Business number, missed-call voicemail and email enquiries land in one queue. Each gets a reply drafted from your FAQ with the questions you always ask, and a lead in Jobber, ServiceM8 or your CRM.
services.human: You approve every first reply. Anything that reads like a complaint goes to you untouched.

services.name: Site visits booked from your calendar
services.what: Once a lead is qualified, visit slots are offered from your calendar, the booking is confirmed by WhatsApp or email, and a reminder goes the day before.
services.human: You set the hours and the travel buffer; you can move any visit.

services.name: Missed calls answered by text, logged as leads
services.what: A missed call to your business number triggers a text in your words asking what the job is and offering a callback time, with the number logged as a lead. Needs a VoIP or Twilio number, not a personal mobile.
services.human: You make the call back. The text only holds the lead.

services.name: Service reminders for annual work
services.what: For businesses running on spreadsheets or plain accounting software rather than ServiceM8 or Tradify: customers whose boiler service, gutter clean or safety check falls due are messaged on schedule from your job history, with a booking link, and the chase stops on reply.
services.human: You pick which job types qualify and the wording.

areas.proof_note: Qualifying against written criteria and drafting replies behind a QA gate is the LeadForge pattern, built for B2B outreach, not a trades inbox.

name: Manufacturing and wholesale
question_lede: Orders arrive by email, stock lives in one system, accounting in another, and they disagree at month end.

areas.name: Order intake
areas.pain: Purchase orders arrive as emailed PDFs and get retyped into the ERP line by line.
areas.hook: Still retyping purchase orders from PDF into the ERP, line by line?

services.name: Purchase orders read from PDF and email
services.what: Emailed PDFs and scans in, validated order lines out. Customer part numbers are matched to your catalogue; SKUs, quantities and prices are checked before posting to SAP Business One, Business Central, NetSuite or Odoo. An order-desk queue screen is an option.
services.human: Orders that pass every check post automatically. Anything that fails waits for your order desk with the reason.

services.name: Order confirmations sent from the ERP
services.what: Once an order posts, the confirmation with lead time and delivery date goes back to the customer from a template, and the thread is filed.
services.human: A person approves confirmations for new customers and anything over a limit you set.

services.name: EDI exceptions cleared, not retyped
services.what: Retailer orders that fail in your EDI provider's exception queue (SPS Commerce, TrueCommerce) on an unknown part, wrong price or missing ship-to are matched against your catalogue and customer master, and the corrected order is re-released. Generating EDI yourself is a separate project.
services.human: Price and ship-to corrections are confirmed by the order desk before the order is re-released.

services.name: B2B web orders mapped to ERP customers
services.what: Where the standard Shopify or Amazon connector to Business Central or SAP B1 stops: orders matched to the right ERP customer and contract price list, and every order the connector rejects worked from the failed-sync log with the reason.
services.human: New customers and orders over a value you set wait for a person.

services.name: Customer forecasts and call-offs loaded as demand
services.what: Weekly forecast spreadsheets and call-off schedules from key customers, each in its own layout, mapped once to your part numbers and loaded as demand into Business Central, Odoo or your planning sheet on every arrival.
services.human: A changed layout is confirmed by a planner before the new mapping is saved.

areas.proof_note: Messy PDFs and scans into validated records: 412 records, 0 validation errors. Tournament data, not purchase orders; same shape, different industry.

areas.name: RFQs and quoting
areas.pain: RFQs sit in the inbox until someone checks stock, lead times and the price list.
areas.hook: Still leaving RFQs in the inbox until someone has time to check stock and prices?

services.name: Quote drafted from the RFQ
services.what: Stock items only. An RFQ arrives by email or PDF; the quote is drafted from the customer's contract price, tier breaks, MOQs, stock and lead times in your ERP, in your template, lines under your floor margin flagged, and filed in HubSpot, Salesforce or Pipedrive.
services.human: A person approves every quote before it is sent and decides any line below the floor.

services.name: Quote follow-ups and win/loss filed
services.what: Open quotes get a follow-up sequence that stops on reply. Outcomes are written back to the CRM so the pipeline is real, not remembered.
services.human: You set the cadence; replies land with a person.

services.name: Drawings and specs read into a quote pack
services.what: Customer drawings and specifications are read for title-block data, BOM tables, materials, tolerances and notes into a fixed spec sheet, and the closest past jobs are pulled from your ERP with their actual cost. The estimator builds the routing from there.
services.human: No operation is derived from geometry. The estimator sets every operation and the margin.

services.name: Quote turnaround and win rate reported
services.what: Quotes sent, hours to first response, won and lost by rep, customer and product family, from the CRM and ERP, in a weekly report with every number linked to its source. Quick only if the CRM already records outcomes.
services.human: The sales manager reads it. The report changes nothing in the CRM.

services.name: Portal RFQ notifications logged to deadline
services.what: RFQ notification emails from Ariba, Coupa, Jaggaer and customer portals are read into one log with the deadline, the buyer and any attached documents, then assigned. Nothing is scraped from the portal; documents not in the email are downloaded by a person.
services.human: You decide which to bid on; the log only records.

areas.proof_note: Drafting behind a QA gate with capped retries is the LeadForge pattern, built for outreach rather than quotes.

areas.name: Warehouse to finance
areas.pain: The warehouse system, the ERP and the finance spreadsheet show three different totals.
areas.hook: Still explaining why the warehouse, the ERP and finance show three different totals?

services.name: Warehouse and order data into SQL Server, nightly
services.what: Ingestion from your WMS, ERP and order channels (ShipHero, Business Central, SAP B1, Unleashed, Cin7) into staging tables, then stored procedures building silver and fact tables, so every transformation is inspectable in SQL.
services.human: Your finance or QC team signs off a column-by-column parity audit before the new numbers replace the old ones.

services.name: Power BI datasets that are not a spreadsheet
services.what: Shipments, stock movements and margins served as datasets Power BI reads directly, refreshed on schedule, with failures logged rather than hidden.
services.human: Finance reviews differences weekly; nothing is averaged away.

services.name: Month-end pack built on schedule
services.what: The exports and pivot tables rebuilt by hand every month become a scheduled job that lands in the inbox with the numbers linked to their source.
services.human: The controller reads and signs off; the job never posts an adjustment.

services.name: Stock valuation that agrees with the ledger
services.what: Built on the nightly tables above. Quantity on hand by location and lot from the WMS, costed at the ERP's method, compared with the inventory account each night. Differences listed by SKU with the movement that caused them.
services.human: Finance posts any adjustment by hand; the job never does.

services.name: Shipped, invoiced and paid matched per order
services.what: Every sales order followed from despatch note to invoice to payment across the WMS, ERP and bank feed, so shipped-not-invoiced and invoiced-not-shipped are listed daily instead of discovered at audit.
services.human: The controller works the list; nothing is invoiced or written off automatically.

services.name: Lot traceability answered from the same tables
services.what: Lot and batch numbers carried through receipt, work order, stock movement and shipment in the fact tables, with the ERP and WMS as sources, so a recall question (which customers got lot X, which lots went into order Y) answers in minutes.
services.human: Quality runs the query and decides the recall scope. Gaps in lot capture are listed, not guessed.

areas.proof_note: Warehouse platform, legacy system, finance team, parity audit: 68,890 orders reconciled across 25 audited columns. A US retailer, not a manufacturer.

areas.name: Purchasing and supplier documents
areas.pain: Supplier confirmations, shipping notices and invoices arrive as PDFs and are matched by hand.
areas.hook: Still three-way matching supplier invoices by hand from PDFs in the inbox?

services.name: Order confirmations checked against the PO
services.what: Supplier order confirmations arrive as PDFs and emails. Each is read and compared with the purchase order on quantity, price and promised date, and the ERP's expected receipt date is updated when it moves.
services.human: Price and quantity differences wait for the buyer. Dates update automatically unless you say otherwise.

services.name: Shipping notices and packing lists into goods receipt
services.what: ASNs, packing lists and container manifests are read into expected receipts per PO line, with lot numbers and quantities, so the warehouse books in against a list instead of a pallet. Built for container imports.
services.human: Goods receipt is confirmed by the warehouse; the list only prepares it.

services.name: Supplier invoices three-way matched before posting
services.what: Invoice PDFs matched to the PO and the goods receipt, line by line, with price, quantity, currency and tax checked. Clean matches post to the ERP; the rest queue with the reason.
services.human: Accounts payable clears the queue. Nothing unmatched is posted.

services.name: Supplier price lists mapped and loaded
services.what: New price lists as Excel or PDF, each in the supplier's layout and item codes, are mapped to your supplier item codes, compared with current ERP prices and loaded with the effective date. Increases above a threshold are listed. Quick only for coded Excel lists.
services.human: The buyer approves the load. Sell prices are never changed by the system.

services.name: Landed cost built from freight and duty invoices
services.what: Freight, duty and brokerage invoices are read and allocated across the receipts they cover by weight, value or volume, so the ERP's landed cost per item is based on real invoices, not a flat percentage.
services.human: Finance approves the allocation rule and each month's postings.

services.name: Reorder proposals that respect MOQ and container fill
services.what: Where Business Central's planning worksheet stops: a Monday reorder list per SKU from sales velocity, open orders, stock on hand and supplier lead time in the fact tables, rounded to each supplier's MOQ and filled to the container or pallet.
services.human: The buyer places the orders. The list is a proposal.

areas.proof_note: PDFs and scans resolved through OCR noise with an 8-tier matcher and a hard gate: 412 records, 0 errors. Tournament data, not supplier paperwork.

areas.name: Quality and inspection
areas.pain: Certificates of analysis are filed unread, and non-conformance reports are written up after the shift.
areas.hook: Still filing certificates of analysis unread and writing up NCRs after the shift?

services.name: Certificates of analysis checked against the spec
services.what: For food, chemicals and pharma. Supplier CoAs and test reports arriving as PDFs are read per lot, each value compared with your specification limits, and the lot released or held in Business Central, SAP B1 or your QMS with the result attached.
services.human: Out-of-spec lots are held for the quality manager. Releasing a held lot is a person's decision.

services.name: Non-conformance reports drafted from photos and notes
services.what: A photo and a voice note sent from the line become a drafted NCR with part, lot, defect type, quantity and where it was found, filed in your QMS (Qualio, ETQ or a SharePoint list) and linked to the supplier or work order.
services.human: The quality engineer edits and signs the NCR. Disposition is theirs.

services.name: Labels and packaging photos checked in batch
services.what: Photos of labels, packaging and shipping marks taken at the end of the line are checked in batch against written rules: right label on the right lot, legible barcode, correct language. Failures are parked for review. Not inline inspection; no camera, lighting or PLC work.
services.human: An operator decides on every parked photo. Rules are yours and can be changed any time.

services.name: Supplier quality scorecard from receipts and NCRs
services.what: On-time delivery, rejected lots and NCRs per supplier from the ERP and QMS, in a monthly scorecard, every number linked to the receipt or report behind it.
services.human: Purchasing decides what to do with a supplier; the scorecard only shows.

services.name: Audit evidence assembled for ISO 9001
services.what: Calibration records, training records, NCR closures and management review minutes are collected from where they live into the folder structure your auditor expects, with gaps listed before the audit, not during it.
services.human: The quality manager fills the gaps and signs off the pack.

services.name: Root causes grouped across NCRs and complaints
services.what: NCR and complaint text is clustered by defect, part family and supplier each month, so the same failure reported ten different ways shows as one line with the records behind it.
services.human: The quality team decides which to open a CAPA on.

areas.proof_note: A vision model checking every item against written rules, verdict and rule recorded, 100+ a day. Built for ad creatives, not factory labels.

areas.name: Shop floor and maintenance
areas.pain: Downtime is logged on paper, the shift report is retyped, and OEE is a monthly guess.
areas.hook: Still retyping the shift report and guessing OEE from a paper downtime log?

services.name: Shift reports read from paper and WhatsApp
services.what: Shift-sheet photos, voice notes and messages from supervisors to a WhatsApp Business number or Teams are read into output, downtime, scrap and reasons per line and shift, checked against counter totals from your MES or the machine-data tables below, and written to a shared table.
services.human: A mismatch with the counters waits for the supervisor.

services.name: Machine data into SQL Server for OEE
services.what: Counts, states and alarms from CSV drops or your MES API first; OPC UA through a Kepware or Ignition gateway, never direct to PLCs. Staging, stored procedures building run, stop and scrap tables, and Power BI for OEE by line and shift.
services.human: Production signs off the parity check against the manual log before the old sheet is retired.

services.name: Morning production digest before the meeting
services.what: Yesterday's output, downtime by reason, scrap and open work orders in one short message to Teams or Slack at a set time, every number linked to its source.
services.human: The production manager reads it and decides. The agent changes nothing.

services.name: Work instructions answered from your own documents
services.what: Operators ask a question in Teams or on a tablet and get an answer drawn only from your work instructions, drawings and machine manuals, with the page it came from. A self-hosted model is an option where drawings must stay on site.
services.human: Answers cite the document. Anything about safety or a deviation is routed to a supervisor.

services.name: Run hours fed into the CMMS
services.what: Run hours and cycle counts from the machine-data tables are written to the asset meters in MaintainX, Fiix or Limble through their API, so the meter-based work orders those tools already raise trigger on real hours, not on a calendar. Needs the machine-data service.
services.human: The maintenance planner schedules the stop. The work order is the CMMS's own proposal.

areas.proof_note: Platform data into SQL Server staging, stored procedures, fact tables and Power BI; 68,890 orders reconciled, synced nightly. Fulfilment data, not machine counts.

areas.name: Planning and engineering changes
areas.pain: Capacity lives in a spreadsheet, standard times are years old, and engineering changes travel by email.
areas.hook: Still planning capacity in a spreadsheet and chasing engineering changes by email?

services.name: Capacity and load view with late-order warnings
services.what: Open sales and work orders, routings and standard times from Business Central, Odoo or SAP B1, plus actual run time from the machine-data tables, built into load-per-work-centre fact tables and a Power BI view that lists orders that will miss their date. Not a scheduler.
services.human: The planner moves the work. The view warns; it never reschedules an order.

services.name: Engineering change impact list from the ECO
services.what: An ECO as PDF, or an export from SolidWorks PDM or Autodesk Vault, is read for affected parts and revisions, and every BOM, routing, drawing and work instruction that references them is listed from the ERP API and your document store, plus drafted work-instruction edits.
services.human: The engineer releases every BOM and routing change. The list and the drafts never write to the ERP.

services.name: Standard times checked against actual cycle times
services.what: Standard times in the ERP routing compared with actual run and setup times from the machine-data tables, per part and work centre, so the standards behind costing and lead-time promises are listed where wrong, with the runs behind each line. Needs the machine-data service.
services.human: Industrial engineering decides which standards to change. The ERP routing is never edited by the job.

services.name: Quoted versus actual cost per job
services.what: For job shops and engineered-to-order work: the quoted material, labour and outside-processing cost beside the actual cost from the ERP job, per job and per operation, in a monthly report, so the estimate rules are corrected from evidence rather than memory.
services.human: The estimator and the controller read it. Rates and margins change only when they say so.

areas.proof_note: Stored procedures, fact tables and Power BI, checked column by column against the legacy system: 68,890 orders. Retail fulfilment, not routings.

areas.name: Product data and catalogues
areas.pain: Specs live in datasheets, the ERP, the web shop and a spreadsheet that never agree.
areas.hook: Still maintaining product specs in four places and fixing the web shop by hand?

services.name: Datasheets and spec sheets read into product attributes
services.what: Supplier datasheets and your own spec sheets, as PDFs, are read into a fixed attribute schema per product (dimensions, materials, ratings, certifications) and checked for units and ranges before they reach Akeneo, the ERP or the web shop.
services.human: Attributes that fail a check wait for the product manager. Nothing is published on a guess.

services.name: Catalogue sync exceptions and price approvals
services.what: Your Akeneo, Shopify or Amazon connector keeps doing the sync. Around it: every failed push logged with the item and the reason and retried, and price changes above a threshold held for approval before they go live.

services.name: Product descriptions drafted from attributes, in your voice
services.what: Web copy, marketplace bullets and translations drafted from the validated attributes and your style rules, checked by a second model against the attributes so no claim appears that the data does not support.
services.human: Marketing approves every description before it is published.

services.name: Product photos cleaned up and checked
services.what: Existing catalogue photos brought to one standard: background removed or replaced, margins and crop set, label legibility checked by a vision model against your written rules, with failures parked rather than published. The product itself is never regenerated or re-angled.
services.human: Your team approves the set before it reaches the shop.

services.name: Part-number cross-reference, the shared resolver
services.what: The matching component behind order intake, EDI exceptions and RFQs, not a separate build: customer and competitor part numbers resolved to your SKUs with a matcher built for typos and OCR noise, so every intake matches on the first pass.
services.human: Low-confidence matches are confirmed by a person once, then remembered.

services.name: Self-hosted product assistant for distributors
services.what: A chat on your site or distributor portal that answers spec, compatibility and stock questions from the validated product data and your documents only. The open-weight model runs on your own GPU or an EU server, so pricing and customer data stay in your environment.
services.human: Anything it cannot answer from your data is handed to a person with the thread.

areas.proof_note: Fixed-schema extraction with rules deciding after the model and an 8-tier resolver for noisy names: 412 records, 0 errors. Tournament data, not product specs.

areas.name: Order status and returns
areas.pain: “Where is my order” means opening the ERP and the carrier site for every email.
areas.hook: Still answering “where is my order?” by opening the ERP and the carrier site?

services.name: Order status replies drafted from ERP and carrier
services.what: Status emails and WhatsApp Business messages are matched to the order, the ERP and the carrier API (UPS, DHL, FedEx) are checked, and a reply is drafted with the despatch date, tracking link and any backorder lines.
services.human: A person approves each reply until you choose to let routine ones go out alone.

services.name: Late orders flagged before the customer asks
services.what: Each morning, orders past their promised date or short on stock are listed by customer, and a notice in your wording is drafted with the new date from the ERP.
services.human: Sales decides which customers to tell and when. Nothing is sent without approval.

services.name: Returns and warranty claims logged with photos
services.what: RMA requests arriving by email, web form or WhatsApp Business are matched to the order and lot, photos are checked against your return rules, and an RMA is raised in the ERP with a drafted acknowledgement.
services.human: Credit and replacement decisions stay with a person. The system logs and drafts.

services.name: Carrier claims filed from PODs and photos
services.what: For the carriers you ship with, each form mapped once: lost or damaged deliveries matched to the shipment, the POD and photos gathered, and the claim form filled and filed within that carrier's deadline.
services.human: You confirm each claim before it is submitted.

services.name: Key-account open-order reports on schedule
services.what: Each key account gets its open orders, promised dates and shipments in its own format on the day it expects it, built from the ERP and sent from your mailbox.
services.human: The account manager reviews before the first send to each customer; after that it runs unless a check fails.

services.name: Customer portal for orders, documents and claims
services.what: A page where customers see open orders, promised dates, tracking, invoices and certificates of analysis per lot, and raise a return, all read live from the ERP. Next.js and FastAPI, hosted where your data must stay.
services.human: Returns raised through the portal still wait for a person to approve.

areas.proof_note: Several live systems read, one plain message written, every figure linked to its source: the analytics agent, built for marketing, not an order desk.

name: Healthcare clinics
question_lede: The front desk runs the book, the phone, WhatsApp, the claims and the paperwork, between patients.

areas.name: Patient enquiries and booking
areas.pain: The same questions arrive on WhatsApp, Instagram and the phone all day.
areas.hook: Still answering “anything this week?” on WhatsApp between patients?

services.name: Enquiries answered from your FAQ and price list
services.what: One flow over the WhatsApp Business API, Instagram DMs and email drafts replies from your FAQ and price list, offers open slots from Dentally, Cliniko or Pabau through their APIs, and logs each enquiry with its source and outcome.
services.human: The front desk approves every reply before it sends. Anything clinical goes to a person, never the machine.

services.name: Reminders and recalls on schedule
services.what: Appointment reminders and hygiene recalls run from Dentally, Cliniko or Pabau on a schedule, by WhatsApp or SMS, in your wording, and stop as soon as the patient replies or books.
services.human: You choose the wording and timing; replies always reach a person.

services.name: Reviews asked for at the right moment
services.what: After a completed visit, a Google review request goes out in your words, once. Every patient is asked; the only rule is a delay while a complaint is open, not a filter on who is asked.
services.human: The practice manager sets the timing and the delay; the system never decides who deserves a request.

services.name: Missed calls answered on WhatsApp within minutes
services.what: Needs a phone system with webhooks: Aircall, 3CX or RingCentral. A missed call or voicemail triggers a WhatsApp message with a booking link, the voicemail is transcribed, and the enquiry is logged with its source.
services.human: The desk sees every transcript; callers who ask for a person get a callback task.

services.name: Cancellations filled from the waitlist
services.what: When a slot opens in Dentally, Cliniko or Pabau, matching patients on the waitlist are offered it in order by WhatsApp or SMS. The slot is held while each offer is open, and the first to confirm is booked.
services.human: You set the order and the rules for which patients are offered what.

services.name: Calls answered and booked by a voice agent
services.what: Calls forwarded from Aircall, 3CX, RingCentral or a Twilio number reach an agent that books, moves and cancels appointments through the Dentally or Cliniko API and hands anything else to a person. Speech models run on your own GPU; call audio stays with you.
services.human: Every call is transcribed and reviewed in the first weeks. Anything clinical or unclear goes to the desk at once.

areas.proof_note: DentaSmile runs in production for dental clinics; the enquiry flows and the voice agent are new offers, not yet a case study.

areas.name: Intake documents and referrals
areas.pain: Intake forms, referrals and insurance letters arrive as photos and get retyped.
areas.hook: Still retyping intake forms and referral letters from photos into the practice system?

services.name: Intake forms and referrals read into the record
services.what: Intake forms, GP referrals and insurance letters, as photos, scans or PDFs, are read by text and vision models, matched to the patient record, and checked against hard rules. Clean records go to Dentally or Cliniko by API, or to an import file.
services.human: Records that fail the validation gate wait for a staff member with the reason.

services.name: Patient data kept in your stack
services.what: The same intake pipeline on hardware you control: OCR and an open-weight vision model on a RunPod GPU or your own server, EU-resident where required, the DentaSmile pattern. Patient documents and photos never reach a third-party API. Same validation gate, same queue.
services.human: You decide where data may go before the build starts.

services.name: Medical history forms checked before the appointment
services.what: Online or paper medical history forms are read, compared with the previous version in the record, and changes in medication, allergies or conditions are flagged on the day sheet before the patient is seen.
services.human: The clinician reads the flags; nothing is interpreted clinically by the system.

services.name: Referrals triaged and acknowledged the same day
services.what: For specialist practices. Once a referral is extracted, it is classified by treatment type and urgency from your rules, acknowledged to the referrer from a template by email, and queued for the right clinician.
services.human: A clinician sets the urgency rules and confirms anything marked urgent.

services.name: Duplicate patient records found once, from the export
services.what: A one-off clean-up. The patient export from Dentally, SOE Exact or Cliniko goes through the escalating matcher that resolves misspelt names, old addresses and swapped dates, and comes back as a merge list with a confidence per pair.
services.human: The desk confirms each merge in the practice system; nothing is merged by the system.

areas.proof_note: 412 records, 0 validation errors on mixed PDFs and scans, with a hard validation gate. Tournament data rather than patient records.

areas.name: Patient-facing previews
areas.pain: Cosmetic consults still run on “trust me”.
areas.hook: Still asking cosmetic patients to commit without seeing their own result?

services.name: A preview app in the shape of DentaSmile
services.what: The patient uploads a photo, a self-hosted open-weight model generates the preview on RunPod or your own GPU, and a Next.js app with a FastAPI job API queues and polls instead of timing out. Workers scale with the queue under a spend cap you set.
services.human: The clinician reviews the preview with the patient. The treatment decision stays with the clinician.

services.name: Previews logged from upload to result
services.what: Each job keeps the input photo, the preview, its status and timing, and who viewed it, under retention rules you set. Patient deletion requests are run from one place and logged, so you can show what a patient was shown and when.
services.human: Your team decides retention and who can see the log.

services.name: Preview on your website as the first enquiry
services.what: The preview flow embedded on your site: photo in, preview out, with consent recorded before upload and the enquiry filed to HubSpot, Pipedrive or your CRM with the image attached, so the desk follows up from the record.
services.human: You decide what the patient sees; the desk follows up every enquiry.

services.name: Previews for more than one treatment
services.what: Whitening, aligners, veneers or skin treatments as separate preview modes on the same worker, each with its own prompt, test set and review rules, so a cosmetic clinic can offer more than one result from one upload.
services.human: The clinician signs off each mode on test photos before it is offered to patients.

areas.proof_note: Built for dental clinics and live: 3 services, ~110 s per inference, queued and polled, photos kept off third-party APIs.

areas.name: Treatment plans, consent and aftercare
areas.pain: Treatment plans are presented once, then sit unaccepted with nobody chasing.
areas.hook: Still letting treatment plans sit unaccepted because nobody has time to follow up?

services.name: Treatment plan letter drafted from the plan
services.what: The plan, from the Dentally API or the plan export or PDF from SOE Exact or Dentrix, becomes a patient letter in plain language, in your template, with costs, stages and the finance options you offer.
services.human: The clinician approves every letter. Clinical wording is never changed by the system.

services.name: Consult follow-ups that stop on reply
services.what: After a consultation or an unaccepted plan, a sequence by WhatsApp or email in your words, spaced as you choose, that stops the moment the patient books, pays a deposit or replies. Patients who never reply are listed for the coordinator.
services.human: The treatment coordinator owns the wording and takes every reply.

services.name: Finance quote and deposit sent together
services.what: The plan cost split into the payment options you run, with the deposit link from Stripe or GoCardless and the booking slot in one message. Finance terms and monthly figures come from your finance provider's table, never from the system.
services.human: The desk approves the quote; terms come from your finance provider, not the system.

services.name: Consent forms matched to the treatment
services.what: The right consent form for the booked treatment, read from the Dentally API or the day-sheet export, is sent for e-signature before the appointment. The signed copy is filed to the record and checked against what was booked.
services.human: A missing or mismatched consent is flagged to the clinician before the appointment starts.

services.name: Pre-op and post-op instructions by procedure
services.what: Instructions matched to the booked procedure go out by WhatsApp or email at the right time before and after the appointment, with a check-in message after surgery that routes any concern to the desk.
services.human: Clinicians write the instructions; any reply describing a problem goes to a person at once.

areas.proof_note: Drafting behind a QA gate with capped retries is the LeadForge pattern, built for B2B outreach rather than treatment plans.

areas.name: Clinical notes and letters
areas.pain: Notes are typed after the last patient, and referral letters wait a week.
areas.hook: Still writing up notes after the last patient and referral letters at the weekend?

services.name: Dictation into your note template, self-hosted
services.what: The clinician dictates after the appointment. A self-hosted speech model on your GPU transcribes, and the text is filled into your note template; audio never leaves your servers. Summarising or structuring clinical content is out of scope.
services.human: The clinician reads and signs every note. Nothing is filed unsigned.

services.name: Referral and GP letters drafted from the notes
services.what: A referral or discharge letter drafted from the signed note and the patient record, on your letterhead, in your wording, ready to file in the practice system and send. Clinical findings are copied, not rephrased.
services.human: The clinician approves each letter before it is sent.

services.name: Phone photos filed to the patient record
services.what: Clinical photos taken on a practice phone are shared to one intake, matched to the patient from the day's diary by time and chair, confirmed by the nurse, and filed as attachments through the Cliniko API or to a per-patient folder your system imports.
services.human: Unmatched photos wait in a queue for the nurse to assign.

services.name: Notes audited for missing fields
services.what: Signed notes, from the Dentally API or a notes export, are read each night by a model on your own GPU against your list of required items, such as consent, medical history update and treatment code, and the gaps are listed per clinician.
services.human: The clinical lead sets the list and reviews the gaps.

areas.proof_note: DentaSmile keeps patient photos on self-hosted GPUs for dental clinics; dictation and notes are a new offer on the same infrastructure.

areas.name: Insurance claims for US practices
areas.pain: Claims are keyed in by hand, rejections come back weeks later, and nobody tracks them.
areas.hook: Still keying claims in by hand and finding the rejections a month later?

services.name: Claims drafted from the completed treatment
services.what: For US practices. Completed treatments from the Open Dental API or the Dentrix or Eaglesoft export become claim forms with CDT codes, dates and fees filled in and checked against the payer rules you give me, before anyone submits.
services.human: The claims administrator reviews and submits. Nothing is submitted by the system.

services.name: Remittances and EOBs read and matched to claims
services.what: Remittance advices and EOBs arriving as PDFs or forwarded email are read, matched to the claims they pay, and shortfalls, denials and partial payments are listed with the reason code and the next step.
services.human: The administrator decides what to resubmit, appeal or write off.

services.name: Eligibility checked through your clearinghouse before the visit
services.what: US practices only. The day before each appointment, coverage and remaining benefits are checked through a clearinghouse with an eligibility API, such as DentalXChange or Availity, and gaps appear on the day sheet.
services.human: The desk calls the patient; the system only flags.

services.name: Claims pipeline: validated, submitted, aged by payer
services.what: Claim drafting and remittance matching as one pipeline, plus what is new: every claim validated before it goes, submitted through the clearinghouse API, every payment reconciled to the fee, every denial queued, and an ageing report by payer. A month running in parallel first.
services.human: Your practice manager runs the first month in parallel and signs off before the old process is retired.

areas.proof_note: Claim forms and remittances are the document-intelligence shape: 412 records, 0 validation errors, on tournament data rather than claims.

areas.name: NHS contract for UK practices
areas.pain: UDA delivery is checked at year end, when the clawback is already fixed.
areas.hook: Still finding out in March that the UDA target will not be hit?

services.name: UDA delivery tracked weekly against the contract
services.what: The UDA report export from SOE Exact or Dentally, or the Compass activity export, becomes one weekly table: delivered against expected to date, per performer, with the year-end projection at current pace and the shortfall it implies.
services.human: The practice owner reads it and decides on diary changes; the system changes nothing.

services.name: FP17 claims checked before submission
services.what: Unsubmitted courses of treatment in the practice system export are checked against your rules: band against treatment items, exemption evidence recorded, open courses past your cut-off, missing dates. A list per performer, before the claims leave.
services.human: The practice manager fixes and submits in the practice system; nothing is submitted by the system.

services.name: BSA schedule reconciled to submitted claims
services.what: The monthly pay schedule and activity statement from Compass, as PDF or CSV, are read and matched claim by claim to what was submitted. Rejections, reductions and late claims are listed with the reason, and the differences are totalled.
services.human: The practice manager decides what to resubmit; the bookkeeper posts the totals.

services.name: Patient charges reconciled to the schedule
services.what: Patient charges collected per course of treatment, from the practice system export, against the patient charge revenue the schedule deducts. Shortfalls, exemptions claimed without evidence and charges taken at the wrong band are listed monthly.
services.human: The bookkeeper reviews the list; nothing is adjusted in the practice system.

areas.proof_note: 68,890 orders reconciled column by column for a retailer's finance team, synced nightly. Fulfilment data, not NHS claims.

areas.name: Lab work, stock and suppliers
areas.pain: Lab cases are tracked on a whiteboard and lab invoices checked against memory.
areas.hook: Still tracking crowns and aligners on a whiteboard and checking lab invoices from memory?

services.name: Lab cases tracked from send to fit
services.what: Each lab ticket is logged when the impression or scan is sent, with the lab and the fit date from the diary. If the case is not back two days before the fit, the desk is warned and the lab is chased by email.

services.name: Lab invoices matched to patients and fees
services.what: Lab invoices arriving as PDFs or forwarded email are read, each line matched to the patient and treatment in the practice system export through name and date noise, and the lab fee compared with what the patient was charged.
services.human: Unmatched lines and price differences wait for the practice manager.

services.name: Supplier invoices checked, then posted to the books
services.what: Invoices from Henry Schein, Dental Directory or any supplier become line items checked for totals, VAT and duplicates before posting to Xero or QuickBooks. Unit prices are stored per item, so a price rise on a regular item is flagged the week it lands.
services.human: The bookkeeper clears the flagged queue; nothing unmatched is posted.

services.name: Weekly reorder list from reorder points
services.what: You set a reorder point and pack size per regular item. The nurse enters a weekly count on a phone form; items under their point go on a reorder list with the supplier and the last price from the invoice history.
services.human: The nurse or manager places the order; the list is a suggestion.

areas.proof_note: The 8-tier fuzzy resolver matched names through OCR noise: 412 records, 0 validation errors. Tournament data, not lab invoices.

areas.name: Practice numbers and reporting
areas.pain: Production, collections and the bank sit in three systems and only the accountant reconciles them.
areas.hook: Still waiting for the accountant to tell you how the practice did last month?

services.name: Practice data in SQL Server, reconciled nightly
services.what: For groups and multi-site practices. Appointments, treatments and payments from the Dentally or Cliniko API, or the nightly export from SOE Exact or Dentrix, with Xero or QuickBooks and your card processor, into staging tables, stored procedures building fact tables, reconciled before use.
services.human: Your accountant signs off a column-by-column parity audit before the new numbers replace the old.

services.name: Power BI across sites and clinicians
services.what: Production, collections, plan acceptance, hygiene recalls and recall backlog, chair utilisation and no-show rates by day and appointment type, per site and clinician, on the reconciled tables, refreshed on schedule.
services.human: You define the metrics once; they are written down and versioned.

services.name: Monday numbers without a dashboard
services.what: A short scheduled message to Slack, Teams or WhatsApp: bookings, production, collections, cancellations and open slots this week from the booking system and Xero, with each number linked to its source.
services.human: You read it. The system changes nothing in the diary or the books.

services.name: Card and plan payouts matched to takings
services.what: Stripe, SumUp or terminal payouts and the monthly Denplan or Practice Plan statement, from their exports, matched to what the day sheet says was taken and to patients and amounts in the practice system, with differences listed.
services.human: The bookkeeper resolves listed differences; nothing is averaged away or adjusted automatically.

areas.proof_note: 68,890 orders reconciled across 25 audited columns for a retailer's finance team, synced nightly. Fulfilment data, not a clinic.

name: Legal and accounting firms
question_lede: The day is email, PDFs, scans and deadlines, and the off-the-shelf AI tools got vetoed on data residency.

areas.name: Document intake and filing
areas.pain: Every attachment named scan_0412.pdf is opened by hand to find its matter.
areas.hook: Still opening every client PDF by hand to find out which matter it belongs to?

services.name: Documents filed to the right client and matter
services.what: Attachments, scans and portal uploads are read, matched to the client and matter in Clio, Actionstep or LEAP with a resolver built for OCR noise, and filed after a validation gate. Duplicates and later versions are recognised and filed as one record.
services.human: Anything that fails the gate waits for a clerk with the reason. Nothing is filed on a guess.

services.name: Key fields extracted into the matter record
services.what: Names, dates, amounts and deadlines pulled from the document into your practice system in a fixed schema, so the record is searchable and the deadline is in the calendar.
services.human: Deadlines are proposed, never set, without a person confirming.

services.name: The intake pipeline deployed in your own stack
services.what: The same intake, extraction and filing pipeline deployed as a product in your environment: a vision model for scans, the resolver, the validation queue and the clerk's review screen, on hardened EU-resident infrastructure or your Azure tenant, with open-weight models, so client documents never leave.
services.human: You set the residency rules before the build and sign off the deployment.

services.name: Scanned post split, read and routed
services.what: The filing and extraction services above, applied to the post room's morning scan batch. The new work is splitting the batch into separate letters and routing each to the right fee earner, with court and tax dates flagged for the diary.
services.human: The fee earner confirms any date before it enters the diary.

areas.proof_note: The same mechanism: messy documents in, 412 records out with 0 validation errors. Built for tournament data, not a firm.

areas.name: Client onboarding and AML checks
areas.pain: New clients mean ID chasing, a conflict search and an engagement letter, all by hand.
areas.hook: Still chasing ID documents and typing engagement letters for every new client?

services.name: Engagement letter and onboarding chase from intake
services.what: The website or Typeform intake becomes an engagement letter in your template, with scope, fees and the right terms, sent for e-signature through DocuSign. Reminders to sign, upload ID and pay money on account run on schedule and stop as each step completes.
services.human: The partner approves every letter before it goes out; a client who replies with a question reaches a person.

services.name: IDV results filed and matched to the intake
services.what: The identity check itself runs in Thirdfort or Credas. Their result arrives by webhook or as the PDF report, is matched against the name, address and date of birth on the intake, filed to the client record, and any mismatch or expired document is flagged.
services.human: Your MLRO or compliance lead makes the decision; the system files and compares.

services.name: Conflict search beyond the practice system's own
services.what: Clio, LEAP and Actionstep ship a basic conflict search. This adds spelling variants, related parties and company officers from the register, and the correspondents in your Outlook mailboxes through the Microsoft Graph API, listing every hit with the matter it came from.
services.human: A fee earner reviews the hits and clears the conflict.

services.name: Company register lookups attached to the file
services.what: Company number, officers, persons with significant control and filing dates pulled from the free Companies House API, or your national register's public API, and attached to the client record, with mismatches against the intake flagged.
services.human: The compliance lead reads the flags; nothing is accepted automatically.

services.name: Risk assessment pre-filled, never scored alone
services.what: The client risk form pre-filled from the IDV result, the register data and the matter type, with each answer linked to its source document.
services.human: The MLRO assigns the risk rating. The system fills, it does not rate.

areas.proof_note: Research, drafting and a QA gate before anything ships is the LeadForge pattern, built for B2B outreach, not client onboarding.

areas.name: Client inbox and calls
areas.pain: Status questions and document chasing are unbilled time nobody tracks.
areas.hook: Still answering “what’s the status?” by hand, as unbilled time?

services.name: Status replies drafted from the matter record
services.what: Routine questions get a reply drafted from the matter or engagement record in Clio, Karbon or your practice system: what is done, what is due, what is needed from the client.
services.human: Every outbound message is approved by a person. Anything that reads as advice goes to the fee earner.

services.name: Document requests and reminders that stop on reply
services.what: Missing-document requests and deadline reminders run on schedule from the record, by email or client portal, and stop when the client responds.
services.human: The fee earner sets what is chased and when.

services.name: Inbox triaged into matters by urgency
services.what: The filing service from intake, applied to the shared or personal Outlook inbox through the Microsoft Graph API. The new part is the triage: each email tagged urgent, routine or newsletter and the fee earner's morning list sorted that way.
services.human: The fee earner decides what to answer; the system sorts and files.

services.name: Calls and voicemails into the file, self-hosted
services.what: Call recordings from 3CX, RingCentral or Teams, pulled by webhook or export, transcribed on self-hosted speech models on your own GPU, summarised into an attendance note and filed to the matter with the duration for time recording. No audio reaches a third-party API.
services.human: The fee earner edits and signs the note before it is filed.

services.name: WhatsApp messages captured to the matter
services.what: Client messages on a firm number through the WhatsApp Business API, not fee earners' personal phones, are filed to the matter with attachments, acknowledged from a template out of hours, and listed for the fee earner each morning.
services.human: Replies with substance are written by the fee earner.

areas.proof_note: Scheduled, source-linked messages are the OpenClaw analytics agent pattern, built for a marketing team rather than a firm.

areas.name: Drafting and document review
areas.pain: First drafts and contract reviews start from a blank page or last year’s file.
