question_lede: A 3PL handles fulfilment, finance closes the month from exports, and the ad account always needs more creative.

areas.name: Fulfilment and revenue data
areas.pain: Month end is three exports and a lookup, and the totals still don’t match.
areas.hook: Still closing the month from Shopify and 3PL exports that never agree?

services.name: Shopify and 3PL into SQL Server, nightly
services.what: Shopify and ShipHero by API, or your 3PL’s export, into staging tables; stored procedures build silver and fact tables; Power BI reads the fact tables. Voided shipments and double-counted orders handled explicitly.
services.human: A column-by-column parity audit runs with your finance or QC team before cutover. They sign off.

services.name: Payouts reconciled against orders
services.what: Shopify Payments, PayPal, Stripe and Klarna payouts pulled by API and matched to orders, refunds and fees line by line, so the bank balance and the sales report agree. Mismatches listed with the order.
services.human: Finance reviews listed mismatches; nothing is averaged away.

services.name: 3PL invoices checked against shipments
services.what: Pick, pack, storage and postage charges from the ShipHero billing export or your 3PL’s invoice PDF, matched to shipped orders and stock in the fact tables. Charges with no shipment, double charges and rate differences are listed.
services.human: You decide what to dispute with the 3PL. The system only lists.

services.name: Month-end pack assembled from the fact tables
services.what: Revenue by channel and country, refunds, fees, COGS and ad spend built from the fact tables into the sheet and PDF your accountant expects, on the first of the month. Needs the nightly sync above in place first.
services.human: The accountant reads and posts. The job writes nothing to Xero or QuickBooks.

services.name: Marketplace settlements in the same tables
services.what: Amazon settlement reports through SP-API, and eBay or Etsy payout exports, loaded nightly beside Shopify with fees, reserves and returns broken out, so every channel reconciles the same way.
services.human: Finance signs off the first month side by side with the old report.

services.name: Refunds matched to returns received
services.what: Refunds and exchanges in Shopify, Loop or your returns app matched to items ShipHero logged as received and restocked. Refunds with no return, returns with no refund, and items received but not restocked are listed each week. Built on the fact tables.
services.human: Finance and the 3PL contact work the list. Nothing is written back to Shopify.

areas.proof_note: Built for a US retailer’s finance team: 68,890 orders reconciled across 25 audited columns, synced nightly. Same platforms, same problem.

areas.name: Ad creative
areas.pain: The ad account is starved of fresh creative because every image waits on a designer.
areas.hook: Still starving the ad account of creative because every image waits on a designer?

services.name: Creative generated and QA-checked on schedule
services.what: Brief, cached prompt, image generation, vision-model QA against your written brand rules, capped regeneration. Runs on a schedule whether anyone is watching or not.
services.human: A creative that fails twice is parked for review. A person approves the batch before it goes to Meta Ads.

services.name: Product shots on a white background, at volume
services.what: From the supplier photo or a phone shot per SKU, images regenerated to one white-background standard with the same QA rules, plus a compare-to-original check that flags where the result differs from the source. New SKUs go live without a shoot.
services.human: Your team approves the set before it reaches the storefront. Flagged images are parked with the reason.

services.name: Lifestyle scenes from one product photo
services.what: A product cut-out placed into generated scenes for ads and product pages. A vision check compares each result with the original and flags where shape, colour or label text differ, before anyone sees it.
services.human: Your brand owner approves each scene set. Flagged images are parked with the reason; label text is checked by eye.

services.name: Ad hooks drafted from your own reviews
services.what: Judge.me, Okendo or Yotpo reviews pulled by API or export, recurring phrases and objections extracted in structured form, then headline and hook variants drafted from them and checked against your claims rules.
services.human: A person picks the variants that run. Nothing goes live from here.

services.name: Creative pipeline wired into Meta, results fed back
services.what: Generation, vision QA, upload to Meta as paused ads through the Marketing API, then spend and results pulled back into the fact tables, so the next brief starts from what sold. Needs the fact tables in place.
services.human: A person approves every batch and sets ads live. No spend without approval.

areas.proof_note: 100+ creatives a day, QA-checked, in production for a DTC education brand in the EU. Same Meta pipeline; a course, not a product.

areas.name: Daily numbers
areas.pain: Every morning someone opens Shopify, Meta, Google Ads and GA4 to answer how yesterday went.
areas.hook: Still opening four tabs every morning to find out how yesterday went?

services.name: Yesterday’s numbers in Slack before the team starts
services.what: An agent with tools over Shopify, GA4, Meta and Google Ads pulls the last 24 hours, reasons over them and posts one narrative every morning, every number linked to its source. A Monday weekly version in your template is an option.
services.human: The team reads it. The agent moves no budget and changes nothing in the ad accounts.

services.name: Contribution margin per day, in the digest
services.what: Revenue less COGS, shipping, processor fees and ad spend from Meta and Google, computed per day and per channel in SQL and added to the morning message. COGS per SKU lives in Shopify’s cost field or a sheet you own, loaded nightly.
services.human: Finance signs off the cost definitions once. The figures are read-only.

services.name: Questions answered from the tables in Slack
services.what: Ask in Slack how a SKU did in Germany last week; an agent with a read-only SQL tool over the fact tables answers with the number and the query it ran.
services.human: Read-only access. Anyone can check the query behind an answer.

services.name: Tracking gaps and spend swings caught daily
services.what: Each morning Shopify orders are compared with GA4 purchases and Meta’s reported conversions, and spend, CPA and refund rate with the last four weeks. When a gap or a number leaves its usual range, a message names it and the source.
services.human: You set the ranges. The check posts to Slack; budgets and pixels are not touched.

areas.proof_note: 4 live integrations, one morning message, running 24/7 for an EU marketing team. GA4, Meta and Google Ads there; Shopify was not among them.

areas.name: Support inbox and returns
areas.pain: WISMO tickets, returns and chargebacks pile up in Gorgias while the team packs orders.
areas.hook: Still answering ‘where is my order’ by hand from Gorgias and the 3PL portal?

services.name: Order status replies with the tracking pulled in
services.what: The WISMO slice on its own: a Gorgias, Zendesk or Shopify Inbox ticket matched to the order, shipment status pulled from ShipHero and the carrier’s tracking API, and a reply drafted in your tone with the dates in it.
services.human: An agent approves replies. Auto-send only for the categories you allow.

services.name: Refunds released only after the 3PL receipt
services.what: Loop or Shopify handles eligibility and labels. This adds what they cannot: the refund is held until ShipHero logs the item received and its condition, and the customer’s return history and open tickets are checked before it goes out.
services.human: Refunds above a limit you set, damaged returns and repeat returners wait for a person.

services.name: Chargeback evidence packs assembled from your systems
services.what: For each dispute in Stripe, Shopify Payments or PayPal, the order, tracking, delivery proof, policy text and customer messages are collected into one pack in the processor’s format.
services.human: A person reviews the pack and submits it.

services.name: Support agent with typed state and QA gate
services.what: The full version of the WISMO slice above: a multi-step agent reads the ticket, looks up the order and shipment, checks your policy, drafts a reply and hands it to a QA agent that checks policy and tone, retries capped at two.
services.human: Refunds, complaints and anything the policy does not cover go to a named person.

areas.proof_note: Drafting behind a QA gate with capped retries and one typed state is the LeadForge pattern. Built for B2B outreach, not support.

areas.name: Catalogue and feeds
areas.pain: New SKUs wait on descriptions, attributes and images before they can go live anywhere.
areas.hook: Still writing product descriptions and fixing Merchant Center errors by hand for every SKU?

services.name: Product descriptions drafted from the spec sheet
services.what: Supplier spec sheets and your product brief become titles, descriptions and bullet points in your tone, with an Amazon version inside that channel’s limits, written to Shopify metafields in a fixed schema as drafts.
services.human: The merchandiser approves every product before it is published.

services.name: Supplier catalogues read into your schema
services.what: Price lists and spec files in PDF or Excel, each supplier’s own layout, mapped to your attributes once, then imported on every update with sizes, units and EAN codes checked.
services.human: New layouts are confirmed by a person before the mapping is saved.

services.name: Feed errors flagged with the fix proposed
services.what: Google Merchant Center and Meta catalogue disapprovals pulled daily through their APIs, the cause classified, and the fix proposed per product, so items do not drop out of shopping ads unnoticed.
services.human: A person applies the fix. Price and availability are never changed by the system.

services.name: Colour, material and pattern attributes from photos
services.what: Where the spec sheet has gaps, a vision model reads the product photos and proposes colour, material, pattern and style attributes as structured output, cross-checked against the spec sheet, so filters and feeds stop missing values.
services.human: The merchandiser confirms low-confidence values; the rest are written after a spot check.

services.name: Product copy translated for your EU markets
services.what: Titles, descriptions and metafields translated per Shopify market with your glossary and claims list applied, size and unit conventions converted. Each batch is written through the Shopify translations API only after approval.
services.human: A native speaker on your team approves each batch. Legal text is never translated by the system.

areas.proof_note: Inconsistent names resolved by an 8-tier matcher and a hard validation gate: 412 records, 0 errors. Tournament data, not a catalogue.

areas.name: Inventory and purchasing
areas.pain: Reorders come from a gut feel and a Monday export; the bestseller still stocks out.
areas.hook: Still placing supplier orders from a gut feel and last Monday’s stock export?

services.name: Stock and reorder alerts from the fact tables
services.what: Days of cover per SKU computed from the reconciled Shopify and ShipHero data, with a scheduled Slack alert when a bestseller is about to run out. The quick first step before the forecast below.
services.human: Buying decisions stay with a person; the alert only informs.

services.name: Demand forecast per SKU with the evidence shown
services.what: Sales history, seasonality, planned promotions and supplier lead times from the fact tables into a forecast table per SKU, with the inputs behind each number visible in Power BI.
services.human: The buyer sets safety stock. The forecast is advice, not an order.

services.name: Purchase orders drafted from the forecast
services.what: A PO per supplier drafted in your template from the forecast, MOQs, pack sizes and lead times, with landed cost estimated, delivered to your inbox or your ERP’s API as a draft.
services.human: The buyer approves every PO before it is sent.

services.name: Supplier invoices and packing lists matched
services.what: Invoices and packing lists arriving as PDFs and photos are read and matched to the PO and the ShipHero receiving record. First step: receiving differences per SKU flagged the day stock arrives; then short shipments and price differences listed.
services.human: Documents that fail a check wait in a queue with the reason. You raise disputes.

services.name: Landed cost per SKU from freight and duty
services.what: Freight, duty and customs invoices arriving as PDFs are read and allocated across the shipment’s SKUs by your rules, so margin in the reports uses real landed cost rather than the supplier price.
services.human: Finance signs off the allocation rules once.

areas.proof_note: ShipHero fulfilment data into fact tables nightly, voided shipments handled explicitly. Same stock data; built for a finance team, not buying.

areas.name: Email, SMS and retention
areas.pain: Klaviyo segments come from exports, and review requests go to everyone, including the angry.
areas.hook: Still rebuilding Klaviyo segments from exports and asking every customer for a review?

services.name: Segments and cohorts from the fact tables
services.what: What Klaviyo cannot compute itself: margin after returns, delivery problems, 3PL and wholesale orders per customer, computed in SQL and synced nightly to Klaviyo or Attentive as profile properties. The same tables feed cohort and lifetime value pages in Power BI.
services.human: You decide the segment rules. The sync writes properties only, never sends.

services.name: Review requests only after a good delivery
services.what: The request goes out through Judge.me, Okendo or Yotpo only after the carrier shows delivered, no support ticket is open on the order and no return has been started.
services.human: You set the delay, wording and the exclusion rules.

services.name: Flow copy drafted in your voice and checked
services.what: Welcome, post-purchase, win-back and browse-abandon copy drafted from your brand rules and best reviews, in structured form, checked against your claims list before it reaches Klaviyo as a draft.
services.human: Your marketer edits and activates. Nothing is sent by the system.

services.name: Subscription churn and failed payments, Recharge or Skio
services.what: Recharge or Skio webhooks for skips, swaps, cancellations and charges that failed after the built-in retries, joined to delivery and ticket data. A churn-risk flag per subscriber goes to Klaviyo; a personal win-back or card-update message is drafted for each lost charge.
services.human: Your retention lead approves each drafted message. Automatic dunning stays inside Recharge or Skio.

services.name: One customer across Shopify, Amazon and POS
services.what: Shopify orders, Amazon orders from SP-API and POS exports resolved to one customer record with a tiered matcher built for typos, nicknames and masked Amazon emails, so lifetime value and segments count the whole customer. Low-confidence matches queue for review.
services.human: A person confirms low-confidence matches. Nothing merges in Shopify; the match table lives in SQL Server.

areas.proof_note: Reconciled order tables a US retailer’s finance team signed off column by column; these segments read tables like those. Finance, not Klaviyo.

areas.name: Storefront AI features
areas.pain: Try-on, a product finder and fit advice are on the roadmap, and the demo times out.
areas.hook: Still demoing a try-on or product finder that times out on the first customer?

services.name: Virtual try-on or preview on self-hosted GPUs
services.what: For apparel, eyewear and cosmetics: the shopper uploads a photo, an open-weight image model on your own GPU generates the preview, and the storefront queues and polls instead of timing out. Next.js, FastAPI and a GPU worker, EU-resident if you need it.
services.human: You decide which products qualify and how long photos are kept. Photos never reach third-party APIs.

services.name: Product finder grounded in live stock
services.what: A few questions, then recommendations drawn only from your live catalogue and stock, with the reason shown. Structured outputs, so the Shopify theme block never gets free text it cannot render, and nothing out of stock is suggested.
services.human: Your team writes the questions and the rules and reviews the first week of answers.

services.name: Product questions answered from specs and reviews
services.what: A question box on the product page answered only from that product’s spec sheet, your FAQ and its reviews, with the source shown. Anything not covered opens a Gorgias ticket with the draft instead of guessing.
services.human: You approve the sources per product. Health, safety and legal questions always go to a person.

services.name: Size and fit notes from your returns data
services.what: Order and return history per SKU, with the return reasons Loop or Shopify captured, turned in SQL into a fit note on the product page such as runs small, refreshed from the fact tables with the evidence count behind it.
services.human: You set the minimum evidence before a note is shown. Needs return reasons captured at the return step.

areas.proof_note: A live three-service product: self-hosted GPU inference, ~110 s per job, queued and polled, photos kept off third-party APIs. Dental, not retail.

areas.name: Wholesale and Amazon
areas.pain: Retailer POs arrive as PDFs, FBA lost units go unclaimed, and channels disagree on stock.
areas.hook: Still keying retailer POs by hand and chasing Amazon for lost inventory yourself?

services.name: Retailer POs read into Shopify B2B
services.what: Wholesale POs arriving as PDFs or forwarded emails are extracted to validated lines, the retailer’s item codes matched to your SKUs, prices checked against the price list, and the order created in Shopify B2B or your ERP after the checks pass.
services.human: Orders that fail a check wait for your order desk with the reason.

services.name: One product and stock table behind every channel
services.what: For brands selling through Shopify, Amazon and wholesale at once: SQL Server as the source of truth for SKUs, prices and stock, pushed to Shopify and Amazon through their APIs and to retailers as their order sheets, every change diffed and logged.
services.human: Price changes and stock overrides above a threshold wait for approval. Not for a Shopify-only brand.

services.name: Amazon FBA reimbursements found and drafted
services.what: FBA inventory adjustment, removal, returns and reimbursement reports pulled through SP-API into SQL Server and matched, so lost, damaged and never-reimbursed units and overcharged fees are listed with the evidence. A claim is drafted per case for you to file in Seller Central.
services.human: A person files each claim in Seller Central. There is no API for that step.

services.name: Wholesale orders followed from PO to payment
services.what: Each retailer PO linked in the fact tables to its Shopify B2B order, the ShipHero shipment, the invoice and the payment, so short shipments, unbilled orders and overdue retailer invoices are listed every Monday with the retailer’s terms.
services.human: Your sales or finance lead chases. Nothing is sent to a retailer by the system.

areas.proof_note: The model proposes, rules decide: PDFs and scans became validated records with 0 errors in the audited run. Tournament paperwork, not retailer POs.

name: Logistics, fulfilment and 3PL
question_lede: Life is the WMS, the client reports and a shared inbox full of PDFs.

areas.name: WMS data and client reporting
areas.pain: Order counts in the WMS, the storefront and the finance report never agree.
areas.hook: Still exporting the WMS every Monday to find out why the order count doesn’t match finance?

services.name: WMS to SQL Server, reconciled every night
services.what: ShipHero or your WMS into staging tables through n8n and the API, stored procedures building silver and fact tables, Power BI on top. Voided and duplicated shipments handled explicitly, not filtered by hand.
services.human: Your QC or finance team signs off the parity audit before cutover. Failed rows are queued with the reason.

services.name: Client reports built and sent on schedule
services.what: Per-client volume, SLA, returns and billing reports built from the fact tables of the nightly sync above and sent on the day they are due, every number linked to its source row. Return rates and claim outcomes are columns in the same tables.
services.human: The account manager reviews before the first send to each client; after that it runs unless a check fails.

services.name: SLA tracking from order to carrier scan
services.what: Received, picked, packed and shipped timestamps from the WMS, first carrier scan from ShipStation or the carrier’s tracking API, in one table per client. Same-day and next-day hit rates computed daily, misses listed by order. Each carrier feed is scoped separately.
services.human: You set the SLA definitions once. The table shows misses; the account manager decides what to tell the client.

services.name: Client-facing Power BI with row-level security
services.what: One Power BI model on the fact tables, row-level security so each client sees only their own orders, stock and SLA numbers. Scheduled refresh, failures logged rather than hidden. The lighter option; the client portal under onboarding adds invoices and an assistant.
services.human: You decide which metrics clients may see; definitions are written down once and reviewed by you.

services.name: Morning ops digest in Slack or Teams
services.what: An agent reads yesterday’s orders, backlog, late shipments and stock-outs from the fact tables or the ShipHero API and posts one short narrative at a set time, every number linked to its source.
services.human: The ops lead reads it and decides. The agent moves no orders and changes nothing in the WMS.

services.name: WMS migration audited column by column
services.what: Moving from a legacy WMS to ShipHero or another platform: orders, stock, clients and SKUs pulled from both systems by API or export into SQL Server and compared column by column before cutover, differences listed by cause. The vendor migrates; this proves it landed.
services.human: Your ops and finance leads sign off the parity report before the old WMS is switched off.

areas.proof_note: Same data, same stack: ShipHero fulfilment data into SQL Server, 68,890 orders reconciled across 25 audited columns, nightly. A retailer, not a 3PL.

areas.name: Inbound paperwork
areas.pain: Packing lists, bills of lading and PODs arrive as scans someone retypes.
areas.hook: Still retyping packing lists and bills of lading from scanned PDFs?

services.name: Packing lists and PODs read into validated records
services.what: Packing lists, BOLs and PODs from the shared inbox or an SFTP drop, as HTML, text PDFs or scans, read by text and vision models. SKUs and customers matched through OCR noise, then a hard validation gate before anything reaches the WMS. Can run EU-resident.
services.human: Records that fail the gate wait for a person with the reason attached.

services.name: Client order sheets imported, not keyed
services.what: Spreadsheets in each client’s own layout mapped to your schema once, then imported into the WMS on every arrival with the same checks. SKUs resolve through the mapping confirmed at onboarding, not a second matcher.
services.human: New layouts are confirmed by a person before the mapping is saved.

services.name: Receiving discrepancies flagged at the dock
services.what: The supplier’s packing list or ASN, already extracted above, compared line by line with the receiving count in ShipHero through its API. Short, over and damaged lines listed the same day in Slack or email with the document attached.
services.human: The receiving lead decides what to raise with the client or supplier; the system only flags.

services.name: Dock bookings drafted from inbound emails
services.what: Inbound notices and attached BOLs are read, the container or pallet count and expected date pulled out, and a booking drafted in Google Calendar or Outlook, or as the expected date on the purchase order in ShipHero.
services.human: The warehouse manager confirms every booking; nothing is scheduled without a person.

areas.proof_note: 412 records, 0 validation errors on mixed HTML, PDF and scanned input, behind a hard validation gate. Tournament data, not freight paperwork.

areas.name: RFQs and exceptions
areas.pain: Carrier exceptions and rate requests sit in the shared inbox until someone has time.
areas.hook: Still quoting rates and chasing carrier exceptions by hand from a shared inbox?

services.name: RFQs quoted from your rate card
services.what: An RFQ arrives by email or PDF; the quote is drafted from the rate card table below and your lead times, in your template, and filed against the client in HubSpot or Pipedrive. A QA check rejects incomplete drafts before you see them.
services.human: A person approves every quote before it is sent.

services.name: Carrier exceptions triaged and answered
services.what: Exception emails from UPS, FedEx, DHL or DPD are classified, matched to the order, and a reply or escalation drafted with the order status pulled from ShipHero or ShipStation.
services.human: Replies to clients are approved by a person; the system drafts and files.

services.name: Where-is-my-order replies drafted from tracking
services.what: Client and end-customer WISMO emails are matched to the order, the live tracking status pulled from one platform, ShipStation, EasyPost or the ShipHero tracking field, and a reply drafted in your template. Querying each carrier directly instead is a standard build.
services.human: A person approves replies to clients. End-customer replies may send automatically under rules you set.

services.name: Rate card kept in one queryable table
services.what: Carrier rate cards, fuel surcharges and your client price lists loaded into SQL Server from the PDFs and spreadsheets they arrive in, versioned by effective date, so quotes, client billing and the carrier invoice audit all read the same source.
services.human: Pricing changes are loaded by you; the table is read-only to every other system.

areas.proof_note: Drafting behind a QA gate capped at two retries, with one typed state, is the LeadForge pattern. Built for B2B outreach, not freight quotes.

areas.name: Client billing and invoicing
areas.pain: Monthly client invoices are built from WMS exports and a storage-fee spreadsheet, and go out late.
areas.hook: Still building each client’s monthly invoice from WMS exports and a storage-fee spreadsheet?

services.name: Pick, pack and storage fees computed nightly
services.what: Shipments, units, pallets and storage days from the WMS fact tables, priced against each client’s contract in SQL Server. Per-client billable lines rebuilt every night, with a parity audit against last month’s invoices before anyone trusts them.
services.human: Finance signs off the parity audit before the computed lines replace the spreadsheet. Nothing is invoiced automatically.

services.name: Invoice drafts posted to Xero or QuickBooks
services.what: On the billing day the billable lines from the nightly computation above become draft invoices in Xero, QuickBooks or NetSuite through their APIs, one per client, with the supporting shipment list attached.
services.human: The controller reviews and approves every draft before it is sent.

services.name: Billing queries answered from the data
services.what: When a client disputes an invoice line, the matching shipments, scans and contract rate are pulled from the billable lines and a reply drafted with the evidence attached. A quick win once the billable lines exist.
services.human: The account manager approves every reply; credits are decided by a person.

services.name: Revenue and margin per client in Power BI
services.what: Billed revenue, carrier cost, storage occupancy and labour cost per client in one model, refreshed on schedule, so you know which accounts earn. Labour cost comes from the throughput table under Throughput and labour.
services.human: You own the margin definitions; the report changes nothing.

areas.proof_note: The parity audit before cutover, 68,890 orders across 25 columns, is the pattern the billing lines reuse. A retailer’s fulfilment data, not a 3PL’s.

areas.name: Carrier invoice audit
areas.pain: Carrier invoices arrive weekly as PDFs and CSVs and nobody checks them against what shipped.
areas.hook: Still paying carrier invoices without checking them against what you actually shipped?

services.name: Carrier invoices matched to shipments
services.what: UPS and FedEx CSV or EDI 210 files load straight into SQL Server; PDF invoices from DHL, DPD and regional carriers are read by a document model. Each line is matched to a shipment in the WMS by tracking number; unmatched and duplicate lines queue.
services.human: Unmatched and duplicate lines wait for a person with the reason. Nothing is approved for payment automatically.

services.name: Surcharges checked against the contract
services.what: Every billed surcharge, residential, address correction, dimensional weight, fuel, checked against the rate card table under RFQs and the package data, with overcharges listed by invoice and carrier.
services.human: You decide what to dispute; the system builds the list.

services.name: Dispute pack drafted for the carrier
services.what: Disputed lines from the surcharge check grouped by carrier and invoice into the carrier’s claim format, with tracking numbers, weights and the contract clause attached, ready to submit.
services.human: A person submits every dispute; the system assembles it.

services.name: Freight spend and recharges in Power BI
services.what: Carrier invoices, shipments and client recharges in one freight fact table by lane, service and client, reconciled to carrier statements, Power BI on top, with the recharge gap per shipment: client billed against carrier charged. One more table on the WMS sync; multi-week without it.
services.human: Finance signs off the reconciliation before the old spreadsheet is retired.

areas.proof_note: The model proposes, rules decide: 412 records from HTML, PDFs and scans, 0 validation errors. Tournament documents, not carrier invoices.

areas.name: Inventory and stock accuracy
areas.pain: WMS stock, Shopify stock and the client’s own sheet disagree, and nobody knows why.
areas.hook: Still explaining to clients why the WMS and their Shopify show different stock?

services.name: Stock parity between WMS and storefronts, daily
services.what: On-hand and available quantities from ShipHero compared with Shopify, Amazon and WooCommerce per SKU every day through their APIs, with differences listed by cause: pending receipts, holds, unsynced adjustments.
services.human: A person decides each correction. The system lists and explains; it does not adjust stock.

services.name: Count variances traced to a cause
services.what: When a cycle count in ShipHero shows a variance, the bin’s transactions since the last good count, receipts, picks, moves, adjustments, are pulled from the WMS log into SQL Server and the likely cause listed with the evidence: mis-pick, unreceived PO, adjustment never synced.
services.human: The inventory lead decides the adjustment; the system never writes stock on its own.

services.name: Days of cover and aged stock per client
services.what: Sales velocity from orders and on-hand from the WMS give days of cover and aged stock per SKU per client, refreshed nightly in the fact tables, with a weekly list sent to each account manager.
services.human: Reorder and clear-out decisions stay with the client; the list informs.

services.name: Monthly stock statement per client, reconciled
services.what: Opening stock plus receipts and returns, minus shipments and adjustments, equals closing stock, per SKU per client, built from the fact tables monthly and compared with the client’s own count when they send one as an export. Differences listed by transaction.
services.human: The account manager sends the statement; disputed lines go to a person with the transactions attached.

areas.proof_note: Multi-cause data inflation and voided shipments traced to root cause in that pipeline, 68,890 orders reconciled. A retailer’s orders, not a 3PL’s stock.

areas.name: Returns, claims and disputes
areas.pain: Returns arrive as a photo and a note; damage claims are assembled by hand weeks later.
areas.hook: Still assembling carrier damage claims by hand, weeks after the photo was taken?

services.name: Returns logged in the WMS, not retyped
services.what: Loop and Returnly already raise the RMA; the gap is your side. Their webhooks and client return emails are matched to the WMS order, the reason classified, and the return logged in ShipHero with photos attached, so the bench knows what is coming.
services.human: Refund and restock decisions follow the client’s rules; anything outside them waits for a person.

services.name: Return condition graded from inspection photos
services.what: Photos taken at the returns bench are checked by a vision model against written grading rules, sellable, damaged, wrong item, and the proposed grade written with the evidence and the rule it matched.
services.human: A person confirms the grade before stock is restocked or written off.

services.name: Carrier claims assembled, then chased to settlement
services.what: For a lost or damaged shipment, the tracking history, declared value, packing photos and invoice are pulled into the carrier’s claim format and filed to the order. Open claims get a scheduled follow-up with the reference until a settlement or rejection arrives and is logged.
services.human: The claims desk submits each claim; rejections go to a person and accepting a settlement is a human decision.

services.name: Accuracy chargebacks answered from the scan log
services.what: When a client charges back a mis-pick or damaged delivery, the pick and pack scan log from ShipHero, the pack-bench photo if you take one, the weight check and the carrier scans are pulled together and a reply drafted with the evidence attached.
services.human: The account manager decides whether to accept the chargeback; the system only assembles the evidence.

areas.proof_note: A vision model checking every image against written rules, 100+ a day, capped retries then a person. Ad creatives, not returns.

areas.name: Client onboarding and integrations
areas.pain: Each new client brings an ERP feed, a retailer EDI spec and a messy SKU list.
areas.hook: Still spending weeks wiring each new client’s ERP, SKUs and retailer files into the WMS?

services.name: Client ERP orders into the WMS
services.what: ShipHero connects Shopify, Amazon and WooCommerce itself. This is for the rest: orders from a client’s NetSuite, SAP Business One, custom API or SFTP drop into the WMS through n8n with retries, idempotent writes and an error queue, shipment confirmations and tracking written back.
services.human: Orders that fail validation wait for a person; nothing is created twice.

services.name: SKU mapping confirmed once, applied every time
services.what: The client’s product list is matched to your SKU master with an 8-tier resolver built for messy names and codes; proposed matches are listed with confidence for review. The saved mapping then serves order sheets and ERP feeds alike.
services.human: A person confirms low-confidence matches once; the mapping is then remembered.

services.name: HS codes proposed for new client SKUs
services.what: ShipStation and your broker already produce commercial invoices and file declarations. The slow part is classifying new SKUs. Each product’s description, material and use from the client’s sheet is read and an HS code proposed with the reasoning and the tariff line, listed for review.
services.human: A person or your broker confirms every code before it reaches the product master.

services.name: Retailer EDI files mapped to the WMS
services.what: SPS Commerce or TrueCommerce handles AS2, acknowledgements and trading-partner testing. This maps the 850, 856 and 810 files they deliver by SFTP or API to and from ShipHero: orders in, ASNs and invoices out, every document logged and failures queued.
services.human: Your ops team sees every failed document in a queue with the reason; nothing is dropped silently.

services.name: Client portal with invoices and an assistant
services.what: ShipHero shows clients their orders. This portal exists for what it does not: billing lines and invoices, SLA numbers and stock per client from the fact tables, and an assistant that answers only from that client’s data. Next.js and FastAPI; can run self-hosted and EU-resident.
services.human: Clients see only their data. Anything the assistant cannot answer from the data goes to the account manager.

areas.proof_note: Next.js on FastAPI, agent output streamed to reviewers, is the LeadForge stack the portal reuses. Built for sales outreach, not a client portal.

areas.name: Throughput and labour
areas.pain: Labour is the biggest cost and the roster is set from last week’s gut feel.
areas.hook: Still setting next week’s picking roster from a gut feel about which clients will be busy?

services.name: Units per hour and cost per order
services.what: Pick, pack and ship timestamps per user from ShipHero joined to hours from the export of Deputy or When I Work, in the fact tables: units per hour by picker and shift, labour cost per order by client, refreshed nightly, in Power BI.
services.human: You define a billable hour and a unit; the report changes nothing in payroll or the WMS.

services.name: Next week’s orders expected per client per day
services.what: Order history by client and weekday from the fact tables, adjusted by the promotion dates clients send you, gives expected orders and units per client per day for the coming week. Plain statistics, not a model; the error against last week is shown beside it.
services.human: The ops lead sets the roster in Deputy or When I Work; the forecast informs, it schedules no one.

services.name: Picker-hours needed per day, sent weekly
services.what: The forecast above divided by your measured units per hour gives picker-hours and packer-hours needed per day and shift. Posted to Slack or Teams and the ops lead’s email each Thursday with the assumptions written out.
services.human: Shifts and names are decided by the ops lead; the message carries numbers, not a roster.

services.name: Carrier cut-off watch posted during the day
services.what: At set times, orders in ShipHero not yet shipped are counted against each carrier’s pickup time and the client’s same-day promise, and a short message posts to Slack or Teams naming the clients and carriers at risk, with the order list linked.
services.human: The floor lead decides who moves to packing; the watch moves no orders and changes no priorities.

areas.proof_note: A scheduled agent reading four live APIs and posting one morning message to Slack, every number linked to source. Marketing numbers, not warehouse throughput.

name: Finance teams and lenders
question_lede: Real transaction volume, several systems that should agree, and a month end that proves they don’t.

areas.name: Reconciliation and close
areas.pain: Month end means exporting from the ERP, the bank and billing, then matching by hand.
areas.hook: Still closing the month from three exports and a spreadsheet?

services.name: Nightly reconciliation, audited column by column
services.what: Ledger, billing and bank data (NetSuite, Xero, QuickBooks, Stripe, bank exports) into SQL Server staging, stored procedures building silver and fact tables, Power BI on top, and a column-by-column parity audit against your current reports before cutover.
services.human: Your team signs off the parity audit before anything replaces the old report; unmatched lines are queued with the reason.

services.name: The weekly pack assembled before the meeting
services.what: The numbers currently collected from four logins (ERP, bank, billing, CRM) become a scheduled report in Slack, Teams or email that lands before the meeting it was for, every figure linked to its source row.
services.human: The controller reads and signs off; nothing is posted by the job.

services.name: Stripe and Adyen payouts matched to invoices
services.what: Processor payouts, fees, refunds and chargebacks from the Stripe, Adyen or GoCardless API matched line by line to invoices in NetSuite, Xero or QuickBooks, with unmatched amounts listed daily and the fee and FX lines drafted as a proposed journal.
services.human: Finance resolves the listed mismatches and posts the journal; the job never writes off or posts anything.

services.name: Intercompany balances agreed before close
services.what: Intercompany invoices and settlements from each entity’s ledger (NetSuite subsidiaries, separate Xero or QuickBooks files) loaded to SQL and matched both ways, with differences by pair and currency listed before the close starts.
services.human: Entity controllers agree each difference; the system lists, it does not post eliminations.

services.name: Revenue recognition schedules rebuilt and audited
services.what: Contract terms read from the signed PDFs, billing from Stripe, Chargebee or the ERP, and the deferred revenue schedule per contract rebuilt in SQL Server each night, audited line by line against the ledger’s deferred revenue balance before it replaces the spreadsheet.
services.human: Your controller sets the recognition rules and signs off the audit; the system computes, it does not post the journal.

areas.proof_note: Built for a retailer’s finance team: 68,890 orders reconciled across 25 audited columns before cutover. Fulfilment data, not a ledger.

areas.name: Invoices, statements and applications
areas.pain: Supplier invoices and applications arrive as PDFs and scans that someone keys in.
areas.hook: Still keying supplier invoices and applications in from PDFs and scans?

services.name: Invoices read into the ledger after checks
services.what: Text PDFs and scans extracted, supplier and customer names matched through OCR noise, and totals, dates, duplicates and required fields checked before anything reaches the ledger in Xero, QuickBooks, NetSuite or Business Central.
services.human: Documents that fail a check wait for a person with the reason. Nothing posts without passing the gate.

services.name: Applications and statements into a case file
services.what: Bank statements and application documents, text PDFs or scans, extracted into a fixed schema, running balances recomputed to catch a misread or missing line, and the figures cross-checked, so an analyst starts from a filled file, not a stack of PDFs.
services.human: Statements whose balances do not reconcile wait for a person; the credit decision stays with the analyst.

services.name: Remittance advices matched to open invoices
services.what: Remittance advices forwarded as email or PDF, each in the customer’s own layout, read and matched to open receivables, partial and bundled payments included, with the cash application drafted in NetSuite, Xero or QuickBooks.
services.human: Cash is applied only after a person approves the proposed match.

services.name: Document intake as an app you host
services.what: Extraction, the escalating name resolver, the validation gate and an exceptions queue built as a Next.js and FastAPI application on hardened servers you control, EU-resident or your own cloud, with open-weight models self-hosted on GPU where documents may not reach a third-party API.
services.human: You set the residency rules before the build; your IT reviews the architecture; your team clears the exceptions queue.

areas.proof_note: 412 records, 0 validation errors on mixed PDFs and scans, but on tournament data rather than financial documents.

areas.name: Collections and receivables
areas.pain: Overdue invoices get chased when someone remembers, in whatever tone they are in that day.
areas.hook: Still chasing overdue invoices from a spreadsheet, when someone remembers?

services.name: Reminder sequences drafted, approved, then sent
services.what: Overdue invoices picked up from the ledger (Xero, QuickBooks, NetSuite), a reminder sequence drafted in your wording with the invoice and amount filled in, sent by email or the WhatsApp Business API, stopping on reply or on payment.
services.human: A person approves every reminder before it goes out. Replies land with a human.

services.name: Ageing digest without logging in
services.what: A scheduled ageing summary to Slack or email: what is overdue, by how long, what was promised, so nobody builds it by hand.
services.human: The credit lead decides escalation; the digest informs.

services.name: Replies sorted: dispute, promise or excuse
services.what: Customer replies classified as dispute, query, promise, remittance or bounce. Promises are logged with date and amount in the ERP or CRM and chased the day after they are missed; disputes get the invoice and delivery evidence gathered and a reply drafted.
services.human: A person approves every outbound reply; the credit controller decides escalation; credit notes are never raised by the system.

services.name: Customer risk scored from payment behaviour
services.what: Days-to-pay, broken promises, disputes and exposure per customer from the ledger in SQL, scored against rules you write, with a weekly list of accounts to watch.
services.human: Credit limits and holds are set by the credit lead; the score advises.

services.name: Collections agent with a QA gate
services.what: Replaces the reminder sequence and reply sorting above with one system: agents sharing one typed state read the ledger, history and replies, pick the next action and draft it; a QA agent rejects anything off-policy, capped at two retries.
services.human: Every message waits for the credit team’s approval; any legal step is a human decision.

areas.proof_note: Scheduled, source-linked digests are the analytics agent pattern, built for a marketing team rather than a credit team.

areas.name: Accounts payable
areas.pain: Invoices wait in inboxes for approval, POs are matched by eye, statements go unreconciled.
areas.hook: Still chasing invoice approvals by email and matching POs by eye?

services.name: Three-way match before anything is keyed
services.what: Invoice lines extracted from the PDF, before anyone keys them, matched to the purchase order and goods receipt in NetSuite, Business Central or SAP Business One, with quantity and price tolerances you set and every exception listed with its cause.
services.human: Within tolerance goes to approval; outside it waits for the buyer or the AP lead.

services.name: Approval routing with write-back to the ERP
services.what: Each invoice routed from your delegation matrix (amount bands, cost centre, deputies) to the right approver in Slack, Teams or email, approved or queried with one click, and the decision, approver and timestamp written back to the invoice in NetSuite, Xero or Business Central.
services.human: Approval is a person’s click; the system routes, reminds and records.

services.name: Supplier statements reconciled to the ledger
services.what: Supplier statement PDFs, forwarded or fetched from the inbox, read and compared with your AP ledger, with missing invoices, duplicate payments and unapplied credits listed per supplier before the payment run.
services.human: The AP lead decides what to query; the system lists differences.

services.name: Duplicate and fraud checks before posting
services.what: New invoices checked against history in SQL for duplicates (same supplier, amount, date, or the same PDF twice), changed bank details, unusual amounts and first-time suppliers, with hits flagged before approval.
services.human: A flagged invoice waits for the AP lead; bank-detail changes require a call-back by a person.

services.name: Supplier master deduplicated before the payment run
services.what: The supplier list exported from the ERP run through an escalating matcher (exact, normalised, fuzzy) to find the same supplier entered three ways, with a merge list proposed and bank details compared across each duplicate set.
services.human: A person approves each merge; the job changes nothing in the ERP.

areas.proof_note: Supplier invoices are the same shape as that run: PDFs and scans in, 412 records out with 0 validation errors. Tournament data, not AP.

areas.name: Credit underwriting and KYC
areas.pain: Analysts rebuild the same affordability spreadsheet from bank statements for every application.
areas.hook: Still rebuilding the affordability spreadsheet from bank statements for every application?

services.name: Affordability filled from statement transactions
services.what: Income, rent, loan repayments, gambling and returned payments identified in the statements parsed under document intake or taken from Open Banking categories (TrueLayer, Plaid), averaged monthly and filled into your affordability template, each figure linked to the transactions behind it.
services.human: The underwriter checks the categorisation and owns the decision; the system fills the template.

services.name: KYC file completed around Onfido or Veriff
services.what: The identity result from Onfido or Veriff, proof of address and company documents gathered into one file; names, dates and addresses cross-checked against the application and the public company register; expiry and mismatch rules applied before the file is marked complete. No homegrown ID check.
services.human: Identity decisions and any escalation stay with the compliance officer.

services.name: Credit memo drafted from the file
services.what: A first draft of the credit memo in your template from the extracted financials, the bureau report (Experian, Equifax, Creditsafe, from the API or the PDF you already pull) and the policy checks, each figure linked to its source document.
services.human: The analyst edits and signs the memo; credit committee decides.

services.name: Policy rules checked before the analyst starts
services.what: Hard policy rules (minimum trading time, maximum exposure, excluded sectors, LTV) applied to each application on arrival, with a pass or fail per rule and the evidence behind it.
services.human: A fail is a flag; the analyst can override with a logged reason.

services.name: Broker submissions read and triaged
services.what: Applications arriving from brokers by email or through your own portal’s webhook are matched to the broker and product, checked for missing documents against your checklist, and acknowledged with a list of what is still needed.
services.human: Acknowledgements use your template; anything that reads as a decision goes to a person.

services.name: Underwriting workbench on your own servers
services.what: A Next.js and FastAPI application for analysts: applications, parsed statements, policy checks, memo draft and decision log in one place, deployed on hardened servers you control, EU-resident where required, with open-weight models self-hosted on GPU so applicant data never reaches a third-party API.
services.human: Every decision is made and recorded by a named person in the workbench.

areas.proof_note: The workbench pattern is DentaSmile: Next.js front end, FastAPI job API, self-hosted open-weight model on GPU. Built for dental clinics, not lenders.

areas.name: Loan servicing and arrears
areas.pain: Repayments, direct debit failures and arrears letters are tracked across a loan system and spreadsheets.
areas.hook: Still tracking failed direct debits and arrears across a loan system and spreadsheets?

services.name: Repayments reconciled per loan, every night
services.what: Bank receipts, GoCardless or direct debit files and the loan book (Mambu, LoanPro or the spreadsheet, via API or export) loaded to SQL Server, matched per loan and instalment, with arrears and balances rebuilt nightly and audited column by column against your loan system.
services.human: Finance signs off the parity audit before the nightly figures replace the spreadsheet.

services.name: Failed payments handled on a schedule
services.what: A failed direct debit, from the GoCardless or Stripe webhook or the bank’s return file, triggers the customer message in your approved wording and the case note in the loan system, with the sequence stopping the moment the payment lands. Retries stay with GoCardless.
services.human: Wording and timing are approved by compliance; a reply always reaches a person.

services.name: Arrears letters drafted and queued for review
services.what: Regulatory arrears notices and letters generated from the loan data on the statutory day, in your approved templates, with the batch queued for sign-off before sending by post provider or email.
services.human: A person approves every batch; forbearance and default decisions are human.

services.name: Arrears and exposure dashboard in Power BI
services.what: Arrears buckets, roll rates, exposure and concentration per product and cohort from the reconciled loan tables, refreshed on schedule in Power BI, with movements between buckets flagged the day they occur.
services.human: The portfolio manager decides the action; the dashboard flags.

services.name: Covenant tests from borrowers’ quarterly accounts
services.what: For commercial lending: management accounts and compliance certificates arriving as PDFs are read, the covenant ratios (leverage, interest cover, LTV) recomputed against each facility’s terms, and a headroom or breach note produced per borrower, each figure linked to the page.
services.human: The relationship manager decides what to do about a breach; the system computes and flags.

services.name: Borrower questions answered from the account
services.what: Balance, next payment and statement requests from borrowers by email or on the WhatsApp Business API get a reply drafted from the loan record, in your wording.
services.human: Replies are approved by a person; anything about hardship goes straight to a human.

areas.proof_note: The per-loan nightly rebuild is the ShipHero pipeline: staging, stored procedures, parity audit alongside the client’s QC team. Orders, not loans.

areas.name: Consolidation, cash and ERP migration
areas.pain: Group numbers consolidated in Excel, a week-old cash forecast, and an ERP move nobody trusts yet.
areas.hook: Still consolidating the group in Excel and dreading the move off Xero?

services.name: Group consolidation with FX and eliminations
services.what: Each entity’s trial balance (NetSuite subsidiaries, Xero, QuickBooks or Sage files) loaded to SQL Server, mapped to one chart of accounts, translated at your FX rates, intercompany eliminated, and the consolidated P&L and balance sheet in Power BI, audited against the Excel pack before cutover.
services.human: The group controller owns the mapping and FX rates and signs off the parity audit against the Excel pack.

services.name: Variance commentary drafted, numbers linked
services.what: Budget versus actual by cost centre pulled from the ERP and the budget sheet on schedule, and a short commentary drafted for each material variance, linked to the ledger lines behind it.
services.human: The FP&A lead edits before anything reaches the board.

services.name: Daily cash position across every bank
services.what: Balances and transactions from every bank account, via Open Banking (TrueLayer, Plaid) or statement exports, consolidated each morning by entity and currency, with large or unexpected movements listed.
services.human: Treasury decisions stay with a person; the position is read-only.

services.name: 13-week cash forecast refreshed from the ledger
services.what: Receivables, payables, payroll and scheduled payments from the ERP rolled into a 13-week forecast that rebuilds nightly, with your assumptions kept in one editable table and last week’s forecast kept for comparison.
services.human: You own the assumptions; the forecast shows, it does not decide.

services.name: ERP migration with a parity audit
services.what: Xero or QuickBooks to NetSuite or Business Central: customers, suppliers, open items, opening balances and history pulled from the old ledger’s export, mapped to the new chart of accounts, loaded through the new ERP’s import templates or API, and audited column by column before go-live.
services.human: Your finance team signs off the mapping and the parity audit; go-live is your call, not the script’s.

areas.proof_note: Parity audit before cutover is the proven step: 68,890 orders, 25 columns, verified with the client’s QC team. Retail fulfilment, not group accounts.

areas.name: Audit and controls
areas.pain: Audit evidence is gathered by hand, and AI-assisted figures need a trail auditors can read.
areas.hook: Still gathering audit evidence by hand, with AI tools that leave no trail?

services.name: Audit evidence packs assembled on request
services.what: For each sampled transaction, the invoice PDF, PO, approval trail, bank line and journal are pulled from the ERP, the document store (SharePoint, Google Drive) and the inbox into one indexed pack, with every step and source logged.
services.human: The controller reviews each pack before it goes to the auditors.

services.name: Journal and expense anomalies flagged weekly
services.what: Manual journals, round amounts, period-end postings, reversals after close and expense claims outside policy checked against rules in SQL each week, from the ERP’s journal export, with hits listed by poster and account.
services.human: The controller decides what to investigate; the list is advice.

services.name: Control checks run and logged every day
services.what: Segregation-of-duties conflicts from your role matrix, master-data edits and posting-period changes pulled from the audit log of NetSuite, Business Central or Sage Intacct daily, checked against your control list, and exceptions written to a log an auditor can read.
services.human: Exceptions go to the control owner; the system records, it does not block.

services.name: User access reviews from ERP role exports
services.what: Each quarter the user and role export from the ERP is compared with the HR leavers and movers list, every account with more access than its role allows, or belonging to someone who has left, listed for the owner to sign.
services.human: The control owner signs the review and removes access; the system lists, it changes no permissions.

areas.proof_note: The analytics agent runs on a hardened EU server with logged tool calls, every number linked to its source. Marketing data, not a ledger.

name: Real estate and property management
question_lede: Enquiries from portals, email and WhatsApp; leases and inspections as scans; owner statements once a month.

areas.name: Enquiries and viewings
areas.pain: Portal enquiries land at night and the lead books a viewing elsewhere by morning.
areas.hook: Still answering portal enquiries one by one, after the lead has moved on?

services.name: Enquiries scored, routed and answered with viewing slots
services.what: Portal lead emails, website forms and WhatsApp enquiries are read, scored against your criteria and written to your CRM. A reply is drafted with viewing slots from the diary. Portals are read from the lead email they send; nothing is scraped.
services.human: A negotiator approves every first reply. Enquiries below your line go to a person, not the machine.

services.name: Viewing confirmations and follow-ups
services.what: Confirmations, reminders and after-viewing follow-ups run on schedule by email, SMS or WhatsApp and stop on reply. Feedback is summarised and filed against applicant and property in the CRM, and a landlord or vendor update is drafted from it.
services.human: The negotiator sets the cadence, handles any reply and edits the landlord update before it goes.

services.name: Applicant matching for spreadsheet-run agencies
services.what: For agencies keeping applicants in a spreadsheet or inbox; Reapit and Alto match natively. When a property goes live, applicants whose budget, area and move date fit get a drafted alert by email or WhatsApp, and the match is logged on both records.
services.human: The negotiator approves the send list before anyone is messaged.

services.name: Valuation requests answered and booked
services.what: Market appraisal requests from your website form, portal lead emails and WhatsApp are logged to the CRM with the address and the owner's timing, a reply drafted with appraisal slots from the diary, and a reminder sent the day before.
services.human: A valuer approves the reply and the slot. No figure is ever quoted by the system.

areas.proof_note: Scoring against a profile and drafting behind a QA gate is the LeadForge pattern, built for B2B outreach, not lettings.

areas.name: Tenant requests and maintenance
areas.pain: Maintenance requests arrive by WhatsApp, phone and email and get retyped into a sheet.
areas.hook: Still retyping tenant requests out of WhatsApp and chasing contractors by hand?

services.name: Requests logged from WhatsApp, email and phone notes
services.what: Each request from your WhatsApp Business number, email or phone notes is classified, matched to property and tenancy, and logged with photos in Fixflo, Arthur or Buildium, or by email and CSV where there is no open API. Photos set the suggested trade and urgency.
services.human: Urgent categories are escalated to a person immediately. The manager can override any suggested urgency.

services.name: Contractor dispatch and follow-up
services.what: The right contractor is messaged with the job details and access notes by email or WhatsApp, chased until they confirm, and the tenant and landlord updated at each step from the log in your PM software.
services.human: Spend above a limit you set waits for approval.

services.name: Landlord approval requested with quote and photos
services.what: When a job passes the landlord's limit, one message is drafted with the contractor's quote PDF, the tenant's photos, the repair history for that property and the contractor's earliest date. The reply, yes or no, is logged against the job.
services.human: The property manager sends it. The landlord's decision is read by a person before work is booked.

services.name: Contractor quotes and invoices checked against the job
services.what: Quote and invoice PDFs from contractors are read, matched to the work order and property, and checked against the agreed rate and the landlord's approval limit before posting to Xero, QuickBooks or your PM software.
services.human: Anything over the limit or outside the rate waits for the property manager. Nothing posts on a guess.

areas.proof_note: Multi-source intake with scheduled, logged actions is the OpenClaw shape; that system served a marketing team, not a property manager.

areas.name: Leases, inspections and owner statements
areas.pain: Leases are typed in from scans and owner statements go wrong when an invoice is missed.
areas.hook: Still typing deposit amounts and inspection dates in from scans?

services.name: Leases and inspection reports read into the system
services.what: Leases, inventories, inspection reports, IDs and proof of income, scans included, are extracted to names, dates, rent and deposit and pass a validation gate before Reapit, Alto, Arthur or Buildium is written to. Models can run on your own server or EU-resident infrastructure.
services.human: Documents that fail are queued with the reason for a person to check.

services.name: Owner statements from a reconciled ledger
services.what: One pipeline: Reapit, Alto, Arthur, Buildium or AppFolio exports and your Xero or QuickBooks ledger into SQL Server via n8n, silver and fact tables, rent, invoices and bank lines reconciled line by line, owner statements in your template, every figure traceable to its source.
services.human: Your accounts team signs off a parity audit against current statements before cutover, then releases each month after reconciliation passes.

services.name: AML and identity packs behind a validation gate
services.what: For landlords, vendors and buyers: ID, proof of address and source of funds, as PDFs or photos, extracted into one schema, cross-checked for names, dates and expiry, and filed to the CRM with what is missing. Right to Rent packs for tenants where it applies.
services.human: Staff confirm identity and sign the risk assessment. The model assembles the pack; it never clears anyone.

services.name: Referencing results filed and next steps drafted
services.what: Reports from Goodlord, Vouch, HomeLet or your screening provider arrive as PDF or email. Decision, conditions and any guarantor requirement are read and filed to the applicant in Reapit, Alto or your CRM, and the next message to applicant and landlord is drafted.
services.human: A person accepts or declines the applicant and sends both messages.

services.name: Landlord onboarding pack chased and filed
services.what: Signed terms of business from DocuSign or Signable by webhook, the property form and bank details are read and written to the PM software after a validation gate. Missing items, certificates included, are chased by email on a schedule until the file is complete.
services.human: The property manager approves the landlord record before the property is marketed.

areas.proof_note: Messy scans into validated records, 412 records and 0 validation errors. Tournament data, not leases.

areas.name: Listings and property marketing
areas.pain: Every new instruction needs copy, social posts and a feed check, all done by hand.
areas.hook: Still writing every listing from scratch and finding feed errors from the portal email?

services.name: Listing description drafted in your house style
services.what: Photos, floor plan and CRM record in; a draft in your house style out, with bedrooms, floor area, rent and energy rating taken from the record, never guessed. Only worth it if the built-in copy in Alto, Reapit or Street does not sound like you.
services.human: The negotiator edits and approves. Nothing is published by the system.

services.name: Instagram and Facebook cards for new instructions
services.what: When an instruction goes live, branded image cards are generated from your templates with the photos and facts from the record, checked by a vision model against your brand rules, regenerated on failure with a cap, and queued as a batch. Images only; no video.
services.human: A card that fails twice is parked. A person approves each batch before posting.

services.name: CRM listings checked before the portal feed
services.what: Before each feed push, every live record in your CRM is checked for missing photos, energy rating, price, status and availability. Rejection and expiry emails from Rightmove and Zoopla are read and matched to the record. No portal is scraped.
services.human: A person fixes the record; the check only alerts.

services.name: Slow listings flagged for a price review
services.what: Weekly, enquiries per listing from the portal lead emails and viewings from the CRM are compared with your branch's usual rate at that price band. Listings falling behind are listed with the figures, and a vendor or landlord message is drafted in your wording.
services.human: The negotiator decides whether to raise a price change. The system never suggests a figure.

areas.proof_note: Image generation behind a vision QA gate with capped retries, 100+ a day. Built for an EU education brand, not an agency.

areas.name: Rent, arrears and renewals
areas.pain: Late rent is spotted from a bank export and renewals come up the month they end.
areas.hook: Still spotting late rent from a bank export and renewing tenancies at the last minute?
